findings.description: Tautology sweep is Python-AST-only (rglob('*.py') + unittest.mock-idiom pattern matching); 166 of 225 Rust tests receive zero mechanical tautology screening from this tool.
findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed 2026-09-09: across the entire Rust codebase (274 tests as of nikon-fleet-20260909-7b2e), there is zero mockall usage (not in Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/source), zero occurrences of the word "mock" in any .rs file, and zero hand-rolled stub/fake trait implementations in any test module (checked ptp_usb.rs, transplant.rs, sdk.rs, main.rs — the files with the most tests). The tautology pattern this tool detects (configure a mock's .return_value, then assert that literal straight back) has no foothold: every Rust test asserts against real function output or literal captured data directly. Severity downgraded HIGH→LOW: the original rating assumed meaningful unscreened exposure; verified exposure is near-zero given this codebase's mock-free Rust test style. Not pursuing a fix (building a tree-sitter-based Rust detector, or adopting cargo-mutants as a substitute mechanism) because the risk it would close is not present today. Revisit if the Rust test suite starts using mockall or hand-written stubs — re-run this same grep check (mockall/"mock"/stub-impl search) before assuming this still holds.

scope: light review (four read-only agents plus the orchestrator's own reading) of src/ops/*, mcp/, range_policy.rs, the worker and the read-side ops; commits since 84ccd2e; no build or test run

findings.description: apply_transplant dropped every skip reason except WriteFailed: a planned property skipped on the live re-evaluation was neither written nor checked, so the report could read applied_verified with written=[]
findings.disposition_reason: Skips of planned writes became write_errors entries (status failed); the write run is also limited to the confirmed plan (nikon-fleet-20261028-9c4d#05, #17).

findings.description: apply_restore reported applied_verified after writing nothing when every attempted write was rejected by kind (unrestored was computed only with --only)
findings.disposition_reason: All-rejected-by-kind is now failed; a full restore with a few rejected kinds stays verified (nikon-fleet-20261028-9c4d#18, #19).

findings.description: restore --serial wrote ShootingLimit from another body's snapshot (a Z6III snapshot at infinity reads index 1, one shot per burst); transplant refused this and restore did not
findings.disposition_reason: Restore carries Source::SameBody/OtherBody; an OtherBody snapshot skips the never-translated settings, and Source::of fails closed on empty and id-N serials (nikon-fleet-20261028-9c4d#03).

findings.description: A same-body Z6III restore writes 1 shot per burst when the body was at infinity at capture, because infinity and 1 both read as index 1, so the read-back says verified either way; the restore plan does not surface it
findings.disposition_reason: Documented hardware caveat (F25). Not fixed in be50d12: the two cases cannot be told apart from the snapshot, so the plan would have to name the case.

findings.description: undo_set left out a write that errored but may have landed
findings.disposition_reason: write_errors names go into the undo set in both flows, and the set holds only names the restore point has and the body will take (nikon-fleet-20261028-9c4d#04, #16).

findings.description: The read-back skipped written properties whose names contain a volatile substring, silently: AutoFocusPositionPreset is flagged volatile by mistake, so a write the body ignored reads as verified
findings.disposition_reason: Residual.unjudged names what was not compared, and a read-back that compared nothing is no longer verified (nikon-fleet-20261028-9c4d#06). The substring list still matches AutoFocusPositionPreset: it is disclosed now, not corrected.

findings.description: ClockDateTime is not on the never-copy list, so a full restore or undo could reset the camera clock to the snapshot's time
findings.disposition_reason: Not re-checked after the light review: datetime values decode to {"_type":"datetime"} and transplant skips that shape, but whether restore writes it was not established. Verify before fixing.

findings.description: Restore did not check the live range scale; only transplant did
findings.disposition_reason: Restore reads each range first and skips one whose scale changed (nikon-fleet-20261028-9c4d#38).

findings.description: The live range-scale check compared lower, upper and steps but not default_index, and skipped entirely when steps was missing
findings.disposition_reason: A source range without steps is malformed and fails closed; the doc no longer claims default_index is in the live check (nikon-fleet-20261028-9c4d#21, #22). default_index was left out of the comparison.

findings.description: Serialization failure became success with null data via unwrap_or(json!(null)) into Outcome::ok

findings.description: kill_and_reap has no timeout and runs while the queue lock is held, so a worker stuck in unkillable USB I/O wedges every later camera call

findings.description: The snapshot filename embeds the raw USB serial: only the label is sanitised, so a device serial containing / or .. could redirect the write

findings.disposition_reason: Not fixed.

scope: remediation of all High and Medium findings of nikon-fleet-20261028-e5a3 plus Lows in the same files, and of the findings of two cold reviews of that remediation

findings.description: `find_device` with no `--serial`, one openable body and one skipped body (held by ptpcamerad/icdd) proceeds on the openable one, including for `write_ftp_profile`; the only signal is an `eprintln!` that neither GUI shows. 7b2e#05 was recorded fixed. Untested (see #26).
findings.disposition_reason: find_device refuses (BodiesSkipped) when any Nikon body was skipped and no --serial is given; selection is separate from enumeration and tested with 6 select_candidate cases (ptp_usb.rs).

findings.description: The raw-USB vendor path takes no `CameraLock` and SIGKILLs ptpcamerad/icdd and re-asserts configuration 1 on every open; a GUI Vendor Ops click can disturb an MCP/CLI apply or restore holding the lock (the lock exists because a reset corrupts another session). Documented as deliberate without discussing this.
findings.disposition_reason: PtpUsbSession::open takes the CameraLock before any bus access and holds it for the session; lock-before-find ordering pinned by test. The real hardware path is unexercised.

findings.description: The write gate is a hand-typed `["Z 9","Z6_3"]`, one of five unlinked model lists, with no firmware dimension although the captures were firmware-specific; reads only warn for an unconfirmed model (warning invisible in both GUIs).
findings.disposition_reason: The write gate is the pub FTP_WRITE_CONFIRMED_MODELS, tested as a subset of ops::cameras::KNOWN_MODELS and pinned literally; read warnings come from the same registry and are returned as data (and shown by both GUIs). Residual: no firmware dimension, because the docs do not record which firmware each write was confirmed on.

findings.description: The FTP-profile write cannot be self-verified: slot 0 is hard-coded (every write overwrites it), the 82-byte block is copied from one capture and contains a MAC-shaped value and bytes that decode to 192.168.66.87, the original test rig's Z 9 address, shipped to every camera; limits are guesses; no read-back; `RESP_OK` is trusted as proof. The 331-byte capture variant is not modelled.
findings.disposition_reason: Partly addressed: the 82-byte block is decoded (placeholders, 192.168.66.87/24 of the capture rig) and the network tail is now a parameter, RESP_OK is documented as the only ack. Still needs hardware: what the camera does with the address block, what [0,0] means (slot?), the real field limits, and the 331-byte variant. The default still ships the captured address. Needs a bench session. GitHub issue not filed (public posting; awaiting the user's go-ahead).

findings.description: egui `do_snapshot` re-implements capture and gate and has drifted: capture stats discarded, no `read_ok == 0` refusal, and `NoBaseline` (the Z 5, changed firmware, or empty firmware) is saved and reported "Saved" with no note. The shared op, the CLI and the MCP worker all have the guard. The Python GUI's snapshot path similarly discards the gate verdict.
findings.disposition_reason: The egui GUI runs discover/snapshot through the CLI (shared capture op and gate): read_ok == 0 is an error, NoBaseline is a warning with its reason, capture stats are shown. Tests against the library's own CaptureOutcome serialisation.

findings.description: Same-model pairing is by enumeration order and `usb_camera_list()` silently drops unreadable bodies; the GUIs only `eprintln!` a warning and `do_snapshot` pairs with no warning or refusal, so one Z 9 can be stored under the other's serial (2 Z 9s attached). The MCP refuses; the CLI warns.
findings.disposition_reason: Snapshot is refused (typed SnapshotRefusal) for two same-model bodies, a dropped unreadable Nikon device, or a failed USB enumeration; the CLI also refuses ambiguous serials.

findings.description: `fmt_cap_value` shows `value` for ranges, which is 0.0 on stepped ranges (33 of 39 range properties on a Z 9, all WBTune*); the position is in `value_index` (F18). Fixed in Rust (be50d12) and never in Python. The test passes only because it uses the midpoint index.
findings.disposition_reason: fmt_cap_value follows value_shape.rs (stepped = steps >= 2 and a span; position from value_index); tested with a real Z 9 WBTune range at index 1224, not the midpoint.

findings.description: Import silently overwrites existing snapshots, references and firmware (captures are create-new), validates nothing (an invalid JSON file counts as imported), has no size limit, and aborts midway with no report; rejected entries are not counted. An overwritten reference silently changes `check` results.
findings.disposition_reason: Import never overwrites (skip existing, counts), validates with Snapshot::from_json, size limits, whole-or-nothing firmware entries, name-vs-content checks, rollback of rejected units; Python and egui both, with a shared name table.

findings.description: "Confirm Write" sends the current form to the currently selected serial: the confirm state is not reset when the camera or form changes and the confirm text names no target. With two Z 9s this can write a profile to the body the user did not confirm.
findings.disposition_reason: Confirm Write stores the exact payload and target, names model+serial, and is withdrawn on any form or selection change; the Python flow also names the camera and refuses known-only cameras.

findings.description: Three implementations (CLI, egui, Tk) of snapshot listing with the byte-identity reference rule, reference naming, export/import, capture, firmware reads, settings and serial fallbacks, kept in step by "must stay in sync" comments; the egui copies have already drifted from `ops::list::list_dir`.
findings.disposition_reason: egui uses the library/CLI for listing, references, settings, discover, serial matching and capture; Python uses ls/firmware ls/settings --json. Remaining local copies (zip layer, set_reference write in egui) are pinned by shared fixtures.

findings.description: The scripted transport never delivers what real USB does and the code relies on: a coalesced Data+Response (times out; the Response is dropped by `decode_container`), a ZLP after a 16384-byte container (`ShortContainer(0)`), a split header, a short write, or a reply carrying the real txid (`resp()` hard-codes 0). 11/12/13-byte and 16384/16385-byte boundaries are unpinned. Probed with temporary tests.
findings.disposition_reason: The scripted transport now delivers coalesced Data+Response, ZLPs, split headers, short writes and correctly stamped txids; 11/12/13-byte and 16383/16384/16385-byte boundaries pinned.

findings.description: The only check on what `fleet_gui.py` sends is `help.contains(flag)` on a hand-copied list: renaming `--host` to `--hostname`, `--port` to `--port-number` and `--password-stdin` to `--password-stdin2` all survive (mutation-confirmed). No argv Python builds is ever run through the binary. And `gui/test_fleet_lib.py` (94 tests, the Python half of every parity pin) is run by neither `make test` nor `cargo test --workspace`.
findings.disposition_reason: tests/gui_cli_argv_parity.rs runs gui/dump_argv.py (every Python argv builder, dashed values) through the real parser with NIKON_FLEET_PARSE_ONLY=1; flag renames fail it (mutation-confirmed); make test now runs the Python suite (test-gui target); a fixture parity test pins discover.json to the CLI's serialisation.

findings.description: Three serial-matching rules. The CLI and the GUI's inline copy take the first match over {USB serial | bare SDK id | id-N}: with body A (id 1, serial AAA) and B (id 2, serial "1"), `--serial 1` picks A. `ops::target` pins the opposite behaviour with a test; the other two have none.
findings.disposition_reason: One rule: ops::target::select_by_cli_serial (ambiguity refused); main.rs and the egui GUI use it; A(id 1, AAA)/B(id 2, "1") tested.

findings.description: The `settings.json` contract between the two GUIs is comments only: Rust loads once, Python re-reads on mtime; Rust `save` drops keys Python keeps; a whitespace-only `data_dir` is unset in Rust and a real path in Python, so the two resolve different snapshot directories; Python hard-codes the macOS path.
findings.disposition_reason: One settings implementation (nikon_fleet::settings: unknown keys kept, blank = unset, parse errors surfaced, no overwrite of an unparseable file, atomic); egui uses it, Python goes through `settings show --json`/`set-data-dir`.

findings.description: A second firmware-archive loader with a hand-copied `_FIRMWARE_META_FORMAT_VERSION`, no test (it imports tkinter), and different rules from `firmware::list_archives`: validates only `format_version` (`!=`, so `True` and `1.0` pass), defaults missing model/version to blank, lists the legacy flat layout the CLI ignores.
findings.disposition_reason: Python lists firmware via `firmware ls --json` (the CLI's own validation); its second loader and the flat-layout branch are gone.

findings.description: Three snapshot readers accept different files: Python never checks `format_version`; `ops::list` needs `properties` and `transport`, the egui `SnapshotSummary` does not. The Python tests write version-less snapshots, pinning the lenient behaviour; no fixture covers a wrong version.
findings.disposition_reason: SnapshotSummary parses through Snapshot::from_json; Python lists via ls --json and applies the same rule where it reads a file; shared fixture tests/fixtures/snapshot_validity checked by all three readers.

findings.description: The "plain path component" predicate is copied four times; the firmware copy already differs (no NUL check) and has no parity test.
findings.disposition_reason: ops::paths::is_safe_path_component is the only predicate; firmware.rs and list.rs use it (NUL check added); the Python copy is pinned by the same table.

findings.description: `import_rejects_path_traversal_entries_without_escaping_data_dir` is vacuous: it checks `dst/evil_sibling.txt`, so a `../evil_sibling.txt` entry escaping to dst's parent cannot fail it, and it never checks that `good.json` was imported. Mutant: disable the accept filter and use a raw join; all 55 GUI tests pass and a file was physically written outside the data dir.
findings.disposition_reason: Hostile entries now carry valid snapshots so only the name rule can stop them; the good entry is asserted imported; mutation (raw join) kills it.

findings.description: The Rust `accept_zip_entry` depth tests pass for the wrong reason: `snapshots/subdir/foo.json` is rejected by the filename check, never the length check. Mutants `len == 2` to `>= 2` and `len == 4` to `>= 4` survive.
findings.disposition_reason: Depth tests use names that pass the file-name check; four slice-depth mutants killed.

findings.description: The Python `accept_zip_entry` tests are vacuous the same way: dropping the "." rule, the empty-component rule or the firmware depth rule survives. This is the only gate in `import_data`.
findings.disposition_reason: Python accept_zip_entry tested against gui/tests-fixtures/zip_entry_names.json (46 cases) plus extras; the dropped-rule mutants are killed.

findings.description: `vendor_write_dry_run_still_works_without_any_cli_present` asserts `!text.contains("topsecret")` against a hex dump, so it can never fail; encoding the dry run without redaction survives all 55 GUI tests.
findings.disposition_reason: The dry-run test asserts the redaction positively and that the unredacted encoding does contain the password hex, so the negative can fail.

findings.description: `TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT` has no test: replacing the deadline check with `false` survives. The unrecognised-container loop is bounded only by it.
findings.disposition_reason: Transaction timeout is a session field, so tests use 10-60 ms; timeout and zero-timeout tests added.

findings.description: The retry OpenSession's Enforce is unpinned (`resp()` hard-codes txid 0, so a mismatching reply after CloseSession is never delivered), and the Drop-close test's Enforce mismatch is swallowed by `let _`.
findings.disposition_reason: Retry OpenSession Enforce pinned; replies carry the real txid; close_session makes Enforce on close observable.

findings.description: `ftp_profile_missing_fields`: four of six names are untested (host, username, password, ssid_5ghz mutants survive). It is the required-field guard for the egui write, and the Python copy is not parity-tested.
findings.disposition_reason: All six missing-field names tested, plus whitespace per field, from one FTP_PROFILE_FIELDS table.

findings.description: Per-field ASCII limits are untested: the "every length" sweep covers only `ssid_24ghz` (accept side); mutants raising the cap for ssid_24ghz, ssid_5ghz and username survive; non-ASCII rejection is tested for two fields.
findings.disposition_reason: Per-field at/below/above, non-ASCII and control-character tests on every field; limits are pinned literals.

findings.description: `find_device` with one openable and one skipped body is untested and untestable as written (`candidate_devices` needs real rusb devices); see #1.
findings.disposition_reason: select_candidate separates selection from enumeration, so one-openable-and-one-skipped is tested without rusb devices.

findings.description: `send_command`/`send_data` discard `write_bulk`'s byte count, so a short write is reported as success; no zero-length packet when 12+blob is a multiple of the max packet size (the blob length varies with the fields: 268 + 2·profile + 2·host + SSIDs + username + password; 512/1024 are reachable). Hardware behaviour unverified.
findings.disposition_reason: send_container checks the written count (ShortWrite) and sends a zero-length packet when the length is a multiple of the OUT endpoint's max packet size. The ZLP rule follows PIMA 15740 and is not hardware-verified.

findings.description: `read_container`'s inner loop has no cap and no deadline; the length is wire-controlled up to ~4 GiB; `MAX_TRANSACTION_DATA_BYTES` and `TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT` apply only around it, and the comments claim otherwise (7b2e#20/#26 recorded fixed). Needs a misbehaving device.
findings.disposition_reason: The cap is checked on the declared length and cumulatively; every read goes through fill_rx with a deadline and a clamped read timeout.

findings.description: `decode_container` drops bytes past the declared length: a Response coalesced after Data is lost and the transaction waits out its timeout. A test pins the drop and the comment calls it legitimate.
findings.disposition_reason: parse_container returns bytes consumed and rx keeps trailing bytes; coalesced Response and next container tested.

findings.description: The transaction id advances only on success, so after an error the next command reuses it; the 0x90E8/0x90EE writes are `TxidCheck::Unchecked` (ledger W1), so a stale reply is taken as the ack; no wraparound handling. OpenSession is Enforce, which catches leftovers first.
findings.disposition_reason: The id is consumed when the command is sent and wraps; the session is poisoned after a stream-desyncing failure.

findings.description: `select_candidate` takes the first match on a duplicate serial where `ops::target::select_by_usb_serial` returns `DuplicateSerial`; no test.
findings.disposition_reason: DuplicateSerial mirrors ops::target's.

findings.description: `check_against` is `pub` and never checks that the capture and baseline are the same model; the doc says the caller must. A wrong-model superset passes.
findings.disposition_reason: check_against returns Result<_, ModelMismatch>; test and mutation.

findings.description: When the firmware differs from the baseline's, an incomplete capture (including empty firmware, which the CLI and egui fall back to because `DeviceInfo.version` is always "") is `NoBaseline`, never `Failed`, so an interrupted capture is saved with only a stderr note.
findings.disposition_reason: Empty capture firmware is not evidence of a change; an incomplete capture on a different known firmware is refused (CLI snapshot/check without --allow-partial, and MCP capture_snapshot/check with firmware_shortfall).

findings.description: `baseline seed` writes `baselines/<slug>.json` and says "rebuild to use it", but the registry is a hand-kept `include_str!` list: a seeded Z 5 baseline is never read and no test notices a file that is not registered.
findings.disposition_reason: BUILTIN_SOURCES is generated from one list and a test fails when a file in baselines/ is not registered; `baseline seed` says NOT ACTIVE / needs a rebuild.

findings.description: `baseline seed --force` can replace a baseline from any snapshot (a partial capture, a restore point) without comparing it to the existing one; snapshots carry no partial marker.
findings.disposition_reason: seed --force refuses a replacement that drops a capability, a slug collision, or an unreadable existing file unless --allow-shrink; the write is atomic.

findings.description: The known-good set is whatever one capture read, measured only on one Z 9 and the Z6III in one state (the Z 9 B was never attached); a state-dependent capability could make a healthy capture fail the gate.
findings.disposition_reason: Needs hardware: captures of each model in the states a user reaches (card in/out, still/movie mode, lens on/off, USB power) and the second Z 9; seeding from the intersection of several captures is the likely mitigation. A doc note was added to baseline.rs. Not fixable offline.

findings.description: An empty USB serial is used as is where the CLI uses `id-N`; the GUI stores serial "", writes `Z_9__...` filenames, and its match on `Some("")` hits the first body with an empty serial (CLI fixed in 9d7cfd2, restore in be50d12, GUI never).
findings.disposition_reason: serial comes from discover --json's storable_serial (id-N for an empty USB serial); parity test against describe_device.

findings.description: `discover --json` prints the bare SDK id as the serial where every stored identity uses `id-N`; the Python GUI keys on it so a new snapshot never appears in the list it was taken from. The source comments claim discover prints `id-N`.
findings.disposition_reason: discover --json serial is ops::target::storable_serial, with sdk_id/usb_serial/known_model/baseline fields; a fixture parity test pins the Python copy.

findings.description: The Python GUI builds argv as `--flag value`; clap rejects a value starting with `-` (profile name, SSID, host, username, label): probed, `--ssid-24ghz -guest` exits 2. `vendor_argv.rs` fixed this for the egui GUI (165e731). Fails loudly.
findings.disposition_reason: Every user value is `--flag=value`, positionals after `--`; tested through the real parser and the real --dry-run path.

findings.description: Every CLI call is a blocking `subprocess.run` on the Tk main thread with no timeout, and `root.update()` keeps the buttons clickable so a double click starts a second camera session; the egui `run_cli` has no timeout either, so a hung CLI wedges the worker forever.
findings.disposition_reason: CLI calls have timeouts (egui 90 s, Python per-call) and kill the process group; Python runs them on a worker thread, single-flight, buttons disabled.

findings.description: The overwrite prompt is decided by substring-matching the CLI's stderr ("already archived"/"already exists"); the producer is a typed `FirmwareError::AlreadyArchived`. `strip_sdk_prefix` likewise scrapes the first `{` line out of mixed stdout.
findings.disposition_reason: Exit status 3 = already archived (firmware add/fetch/browse), documented in --help; Python and egui key on it; strict JSON parsing replaces strip_sdk_prefix.

findings.description: The download worker thread catches only `OSError`, so any other exception leaves `poll()` rescheduling forever; `export_data`/`import_data` have no exception handling; settings reads swallow every error.
findings.disposition_reason: The Python worker catches every exception (BaseException with busy cleared first); export/import/settings errors are shown; polling reschedules in a finally.

findings.description: All three `set_reference` writers build the filename from the snapshot file's own model/serial with no plain-name guard (a `/` or `..` serial writes outside `references/`), and replace an existing reference silently; the write side is untested.
findings.disposition_reason: CLI `ref set` goes through checked_reference_filename + atomic write and reports what it replaced; egui uses the same shared function; Python calls `ref set`.

findings.description: `do_export` drops unreadable directories and entries silently and reports success ("Exported 0 file(s)").
findings.disposition_reason: Export lists everything it left out with a reason and writes via temp+rename.

findings.description: `Settings::load` swallows parse errors and a later save overwrites the file; `save` ignores errors while the UI says "Data dir: ...". `Settings` has no tests.
findings.disposition_reason: settings go through the shared library; parse errors are shown and never overwritten; relative paths refused.

findings.description: A stdin write error is ignored when the child exits 0, so a truncated password write can be reported "Wrote FTP profile".
findings.disposition_reason: A stdin write error fails the call even when the child exits 0 (CliFailure::StdinWrite).

findings.description: The egui discover/snapshot run the SDK in-process with the `CameraLock` held; DisconnectDevice hangs about 7% of runs (F24), leaving `busy` set and every other process seeing camera-busy. `sdk.rs` marks it a known gap; the GUI hang rate is unmeasured.
findings.disposition_reason: discover/snapshot run as CLI subprocesses with a timeout, and a complete JSON document followed by a hang is salvaged; the in-process SDK is gone from the GUI. The subprocess path and the USB reset happening in the CLI are hardware-unverified.

findings.description: The Python GUI keys cameras by serial alone (an `id-N` serial can be shared by two models) and lists files the CLI and egui treat as unreadable (no `format_version` check); "Set as Reference" can copy them.
findings.disposition_reason: Python keys cameras by (model, serial).

findings.description: `Z6_3_0200.bin` is suggested as model "Z6 3" and stored as `metadata.model`, so `firmware ls --model Z6_3` and the rollback model check never see it.
findings.disposition_reason: suggest_fw_model returns a known model whose slug equals the file stem (Z6_3_0200.bin -> Z6_3), never a guess.

findings.description: `accept_zip_entry` has diverged: Rust's `Path::components()` collapses `.`, `//` and a trailing `/`, so Rust accepts `snapshots//a.json` and `firmware/Z_9//5.31/firmware.bin` and Python rejects them; the docstrings and test comments claim lockstep and that `components()` rejects CurDir (false). Write-path safety holds via `safe_join`.
findings.disposition_reason: classify_zip_entry splits the raw name and applies the shared rule; both languages run the same 46-case table.

findings.description: The 854-line GUI (argv construction, discover, import/export, `_read_write_fields`) has no test file (mechanical sweep: actively edited, 17 commits); `fleet_lib` gaps: `parse_propcode` edge cases, `parse_fw_filename` with `²`, sort order, `fmt_cap_value` indices.
findings.disposition_reason: gui/test_fleet_gui.py, test_fleet_cli.py, test_fleet_archive.py and test_conftest.py added (652 Python tests, run by make test).

findings.description: Two code paths for the FTP dry run (egui encodes in-process, Python passes `--dry-run`), and the field list/trim rules are hand-copied in Rust, egui and Python (keys vs display names).
findings.disposition_reason: FtpForm::build / ptp_usb::ftp_profile_missing_fields and FTP_PROFILE_FIELDS are the single source; Python's form holds no names or limits and checks via the CLI's own --dry-run.

findings.description: No session poisoning and no `clear_halt`: after any transact error the unread container stays on the pipe and the session stays open; the NX doc records that a hung op stalls the bulk pipe and needed `clear_halt`, which the code never calls; Drop then sends CloseSession into a stalled pipe and the next process starts on it. The CLI is one op per process, so only library callers reuse a poisoned session.
findings.disposition_reason: A failed transact poisons the session, clears both halts and drops buffered bytes; a poisoned session refuses further calls and sends no close.

findings.description: A write that fails after the 0x90EE data was sent looks identical (same error, exit 1, same GUI text) to one never sent, though the camera may have changed and the old profile cannot be read back; the MCP has `indeterminate` for exactly this. A false failure, not a false success; a retry is idempotent.
findings.disposition_reason: FtpWriteIndeterminate{cause} when the data container was handed to the pipe; CLI exit code 4; both GUIs show 'the camera may have changed' for it, and for a killed or panicking write child.

findings.description: The CLI vendor-write path never calls `ftp_profile_missing_fields`: all-empty fields give rc 0 and a blank-field blob that a real write would send; the encoder also accepts NUL and control bytes and 33-64-byte SSIDs (802.11 caps at 32). Only the GUIs guard.
findings.disposition_reason: The CLI vendor-write-ftp refuses missing fields before encoding or previewing; the encoder rejects NUL/control bytes and SSIDs over 32 bytes.

findings.description: A Data container's op code is never compared to the requested op, response params are discarded by every caller, and `Unchecked` write ops record no mismatch; OpenSession being Enforce limits it.
findings.disposition_reason: A Data container's op code is checked under Enforce; Unchecked deviations are recorded and surfaced as FtpWriteReceipt.reply_matched_command, which the CLI prints.

findings.description: Only the GUIs read `settings.json`; the CLI defaults to `.` and the MCP requires `--data-dir`, so a plain `nikon-fleet snapshot` writes to `./snapshots`, which the GUIs never see, though the Python comment says the directory is shared with the CLI.
findings.disposition_reason: Resolved by documentation and tooling, not by moving the default: the CLI's --data-dir default stays `.` (help and docs say so; a test pins that plain ls does not read settings.json); `settings show/data-dir/set-data-dir` expose the GUIs' directory; the false 'shared with the CLI' comment is gone.

findings.description: Export/import is an allow-list of `firmware.bin` and `metadata.json`: `source-page.html` and the six legacy flat `firmware/*.bin` are left out of a user's "backup"; Python exports `firmware.bin` at any depth that import then skips; skipped entries are never counted.
findings.disposition_reason: Export includes everything the CLI treats as archive content (incl. source-page.html) and counts what it skips; import rejects what export would not write.

findings.description: `rglob` with no depth limit plus an iid taken from `parent.parent`/`parent`: a `metadata.json` at a non-4-part depth makes `remove_firmware` `rmtree` `fw_dir/B/C`, possibly another archive. A yes/no prompt shows the label; needs an unusual layout.
findings.disposition_reason: No rglob; removal accepts only <data_dir>/firmware/<model>/<version> (realpath-checked), deletes only the known files then the directory, never rmtree.

findings.description: `bin_sha256` and `bin_size_bytes` are never verified by the GUI loader or import, so a truncated or replaced `firmware.bin` is listed as archived; matters for the rollback source.
findings.disposition_reason: Import verifies recorded size and SHA-256 and rolls back a mismatching unit; listing shows bin_present (the CLI does not re-hash).

findings.description: Python startup crashes on odd files: `rows.sort` sits outside the try, so two same-second snapshots with a non-string label raise `TypeError` out of `_scan_known_cameras`; `parse_fw_filename` uses `isdigit()`, which accepts `²` that `int()` rejects, reached unguarded from the flat-layout loop; `discover()` assigns `self.cameras` before validating, so a `KeyError` desyncs the listbox.
findings.disposition_reason: Non-string labels, ASCII-digit-only filename parsing (²), validation before assignment.

findings.description: The snapshot detail window crashes (inside a Tk callback) on malformed data and substitutes defaults silently: missing code shows `0x0000`, missing value `None`, a missing `values` renders `[index N / 0]`, indistinguishable from a failed GET_ARRAY; datetime/array/unknown shapes show a dict repr; the range shows only `value`.
findings.disposition_reason: The detail window shows '(missing)' instead of defaults and readable forms for odd shapes.

findings.description: stderr from a successful CLI run never reaches the user, including the unconfirmed-model warning for vendor reads (the Z 5 is 1 of 4 bodies outside the confirmed list) and the skipped-body warning.
findings.disposition_reason: stderr from successful runs is shown (Messages box / result box).

findings.description: An unreadable snapshot directory shows as "no snapshots"; unreadable references and non-UTF-8 names are dropped; skip warnings go to stderr with no count; row order differs (Rust sorts the full string, Python `captured_at[:19]` plus tiebreakers).
findings.disposition_reason: Listing errors, unreadable files and skipped counts are shown, not 'no snapshots'.

findings.description: The Z 5 is `known_model: true` with no baseline signal in `list_cameras`, the plans or the guidance, yet every apply refuses `no_baseline`; and `docs/verify-a-model.md` tells the assistant to record `known_model` from `discover --json`, which does not emit it.
findings.disposition_reason: list_cameras and discover carry baseline; MCP descriptions and guidance say known_model:true, baseline:false (Z 5) is refused on apply; the guidance test pins the keys against the real serialisation.

findings.description: Export truncates the destination zip before reading any source; a mid-write exception leaves a partial archive over the previous backup (no try in Python, no cleanup in Rust).
findings.disposition_reason: Export writes a temp file and renames it; a failure never replaces a previous backup.

findings.description: The 11/12/13-byte thresholds are partly pinned: a declared-length floor of `< 11` and a first read of exactly 12 header bytes survive.
findings.disposition_reason: 11/12/13-byte declared lengths and exactly-12-byte first read pinned.

findings.description: `Settings` has zero tests; mutants that stop ignoring a blank `data_dir` or change the load-failure default survive. Settings selects where all snapshots are saved.
findings.disposition_reason: Settings tests moved to the shared library (blank, parse failure, unknown keys, no overwrite) plus a GUI-side test that the error is surfaced.

findings.description: The baseline-names sweep skips with only an `eprintln!` when the gitignored `sdk-runtime/` is absent and nothing sets `REQUIRE_SDK_RUNTIME`; a mutant that makes the path look absent survives.
findings.disposition_reason: The baseline names sweep fails when REQUIRE_SDK_RUNTIME or CI is set and sdk-runtime/ is absent (decision function tested at the boundaries). transplant.rs's real-config tests still honour only REQUIRE_SDK_RUNTIME.

findings.description: `fmt_cap_value` index boundaries are unpinned (index equal to length, negative, `<=`): mutants survive; a string or float index raises `TypeError`. Display only.
findings.disposition_reason: Index boundaries (equal to length, negative, string/float/bool/null) pinned.

findings.description: Policy constants are unpinned because the tests use the constants themselves: 16 MiB to 32 MiB, 64 to 65, 200 to 201, 200 to 255 and the `u8::MAX` guard `>=` all survive. Tuning limits, so Medium.
findings.disposition_reason: Policy constants pinned by literal values.

findings.description: The dry run encodes `*` x `chars().count()`, so a non-ASCII password or one of at most 64 characters but over 64 bytes passes the preview and fails the real write (mutation-confirmed with the CLI). Fails loudly before the camera is touched; 3 call sites.
findings.disposition_reason: The dry-run preview fails exactly where the real write fails.

findings.description: The `usb-<bus>:<addr>` fallback serial is printed nowhere, and both GUIs pass `id-N` as `--serial`, so vendor ops on a serial-less body always fail (loudly). 0 of 4 fleet bodies lack a USB serial.
findings.disposition_reason: vendor-read/vendor-write-ftp accept --serial id-N for the one Nikon body with no readable serial. Printing usb-<bus>:<addr> from discover is not done (UsbCameraInfo has no bus/address; sdk.rs). 0 of 4 fleet bodies lack a USB serial.

findings.description: `set_active_configuration(1)` error swallowed, configuration hard-coded, two `pkill -9` spawns on every open. Behaviour-sensitive; verify on hardware before changing.
findings.disposition_reason: Needs a hardware experiment: the hard-coded configuration 1 and the two pkill spawns per open are unchanged (comments added); only the swallowed set_active_configuration error is now reported in ClaimFailed.

findings.description: CloseSession's response code is discarded and Drop can block up to 30 s. Teardown only.
findings.disposition_reason: close_session returns a typed result; Drop uses a 5 s CLOSE_TIMEOUT.

findings.description: `VENDOR_OPS`/`vendor_op_info` are dead (tests only; the drift test hard-codes five consts), `PtpUsbSession::model()` is unused, a doc comment sits on the wrong item.
findings.disposition_reason: VENDOR_OPS and vendor_op_info deleted (unused workspace-wide); doc comment fixed.

findings.description: `FtpFieldTooLong` reports bytes against a limit in UTF-16 units.
findings.disposition_reason: FtpFieldTooLong reports in the unit it limits.

findings.description: Efficiency: every Nikon body is opened to read its serial (4 control transfers where 3 do), payloads copied 3x, magic 16384 and 12.
findings.disposition_reason: Descriptor identity reads use one language lookup (3 control transfers instead of 4) and 16384/12 are named constants. The remaining payload copies are on ~300-byte buffers; not worth changing.

findings.description: "Sorted by code" is documented but `validate()` checks only uniqueness; an unsorted file validates and `missing` comes out unsorted (probed). Shipped baselines are sorted.
findings.disposition_reason: validate() enforces ascending order (NotSorted).

findings.description: Doc drift (it says apply refuses an unjudged capture; `AllowPartial` exists), `MissingCapability` duplicates `BaselineCapability`, `GateOutcome::tag()` unused, plural phrasing duplicated.
findings.disposition_reason: Doc drift corrected, MissingCapability aliased, unused GateOutcome::tag() removed, shared phrase helper.

findings.description: The Python port parse accepts `2_1`, `+21` and non-ASCII digits that Rust rejects; the CLI receives the normalised value; port 0 is accepted by both GUIs.
findings.disposition_reason: parse_port takes ASCII digits only, 1..65535 (stricter than Rust's u16 parse, which accepts +21).

findings.description: After a zero-camera discover `self.selected` keeps the old index and `take_snapshot` / `VendorOpsWindow` raise `IndexError` in a Tk callback. No data effect.
findings.disposition_reason: A zero-camera discover clears the selection; take_snapshot/VendorOpsWindow guarded.

findings.description: Efficiency: the egui `list_snapshots` re-parses every snapshot per click, export reads whole firmware files into memory, a spinner repaints every frame, Python parses twice at launch.
findings.disposition_reason: The listing is cached; no per-click re-parse; spinner replaced; firmware streamed on export.

findings.description: Small items: dead `_fw_meta`, three copies of the macOS default path, a flat-layout branch the CLI ignores, hard-coded example model strings, no `NIKON_FLEET_CLI` override in Python, a 400-line `update()`.
findings.disposition_reason: Dead code and copies removed, NIKON_FLEET_CLI override and stale-binary warning added in Python, egui update() split.

findings.description: `parse_propcode("5010")` is read as decimal 5010 (0x1392), not the documented 0x5010. Read-only; documented decimal acceptance.
findings.disposition_reason: Bare digits are decimal by documented contract (the Python GUI agrees; the CLI echoes the resolved 0x...). Pinned with a test.

findings.description: The 331-byte 0x90EE variant (an extra optional UTF-16 field, port 56171) is not modelled; the "byte-for-byte" claim holds for two of three captures.
findings.disposition_reason: The 331-byte 0x90EE variant's extra optional field has no tag or semantics in the docs; needs another capture or a bench experiment. The 'byte-for-byte' claims now say two of three captures.

findings.description: The interrupt IN endpoint is never opened, so PTP events (DevicePropChanged) never arrive and the Event arm is unreachable; unknown container kinds are skipped without a counter.
findings.disposition_reason: An unrecognised-container counter exists; opening the interrupt IN endpoint (PTP events) needs hardware and a design.

findings.description: `payload.len() as u32` wraps above 4 GiB and `encode_command` accepts any number of params; unreachable today.
findings.disposition_reason: Checked u32 container length (ContainerTooLarge); more than 5 params is TooManyCommandParams.

findings.description: Descriptor read failures collapse to `""` or the topology fallback serial, `rusb` errors are discarded, and `read_vendor_property` returns `Ok(empty)` when no Data container arrived.
findings.disposition_reason: An OK reply with no data container is NoDataPhase; descriptor read failures are collected as warnings. USB enumeration errors in sdk::nikon_usb_devices are still swallowed (sdk.rs).

findings.description: Only 13 PTP response codes are named; others print as hex.
findings.disposition_reason: All 32 standard PTP response codes are named.

findings.description: The Drop-close test replies with txid 0 against an expected 1, so the Enforce mismatch is swallowed by `let _`; mutating Enforce to Unchecked on close survives. Equivalent by design.
findings.disposition_reason: The drop-close test uses a correctly stamped txid so the Enforce check is exercised.

findings.description: `model_slug` replacing only the first space, `_plain_name_component` without the backslash/NUL rules, and the range branch without `upper` survive; exposure macOS-only and no two-space model.
findings.disposition_reason: Two-space model_slug, backslash/NUL in the plain-name rule, and the range branch without upper pinned.

findings.description: A vendor-write child that dies by signal or panics after sending data was shown as an ordinary failure with no 'camera may have changed' warning
findings.disposition_reason: Both GUIs treat every outcome other than exit 1/2 of a real write as 'the camera may have changed'; tests kill/panic the fake CLI.

findings.description: Import left an orphan source-page.html when firmware.bin was rejected
findings.disposition_reason: A rejected file takes the whole firmware entry with it; nothing is left on disk or counted as imported.

findings.description: baseline seed --force was a truncating write
findings.disposition_reason: Uses write_atomic.

findings.description: write_atomic used a pid-only temp name, did not fsync, and replaced a symlinked file with a regular file
findings.disposition_reason: Unique temp names, fsync, and the symlink target is replaced; tests for a symlink and eight concurrent writers.

findings.description: Import trusted content over name: a reference under the wrong name, firmware metadata not tied to its directory or binary
findings.disposition_reason: Reference name must equal checked_reference_filename of its content; metadata model/version must match the directory; size and SHA-256 checked, rolled back on mismatch.

findings.description: The snapshot list followed the file-name sort, so the newest snapshot was not first
findings.disposition_reason: Sorted by captured_at descending, ties by file name; test with five snapshots whose file-name order differs.

findings.description: The hidden global --parse-only flag turned any command, including restore, into a silent exit 0
findings.disposition_reason: Replaced by the environment variable NIKON_FLEET_PARSE_ONLY=1 (only the value 1); tested that the flag no longer exists.

findings.description: _write_new left a truncated file when a write failed, and a truncated metadata.json made re-import say 'already present' forever
findings.disposition_reason: Staged temp + fsync + os.link publish; tests with a real RLIMIT_FSIZE write failure.

findings.description: Export failed for a file with a pre-1980 mtime
findings.disposition_reason: strict_timestamps=False; test with mtime 0.

findings.description: Firmware import could clobber or delete files it did not create (rename over firmware.bin, cleanup of a foreign .part) and ran concurrently with a download
findings.disposition_reason: No-clobber publish, only created paths removed, one archive-writing operation at a time.

findings.description: remove_firmware_entry was anchored to the CLI-reported dir
findings.disposition_reason: Anchored to <data_dir>/firmware with a realpath check.

findings.description: The vendor-write confirm did not name the camera, and a known-only (never discovered) camera could be written to via id-N
findings.disposition_reason: The confirm names model+serial; the write is disabled for a camera not seen by Discover this session.

findings.description: Text fields were stripped before being sent, which the CLI does not do
findings.disposition_reason: Values reach argv and stdin as typed.

findings.description: Doubled 'Error: Error:' prefix; polling could wedge if the error handler raised; JobRunner caught only Exception; a wrong _apply_cameras docstring; ref_set_argv with no data dir raised TypeError
findings.disposition_reason: Each fixed and tested.

findings.description: find_cli could silently run a stale release binary
findings.disposition_reason: A visible warning when the binary is older than src/**/*.rs.

findings.description: GUI tests skipped silently without a display or binary; the fake CLI defaulted to success; a timeout test was not a boundary
findings.disposition_reason: CI/REQUIRE_DISPLAY/REQUIRE_CLI make the skips failures; unspecified fake commands exit 99; real boundary test.

findings.description: restore targets the snapshot's own serial, which can be an id-N or bare number (an SDK id of the current session); with two same-model bodies a restore can land on the wrong body, and a GUI snapshot resolves id-N in a second SDK session
findings.disposition_reason: Pre-existing, not a regression: select_by_cli_serial refuses ambiguity but cannot disambiguate two serial-less bodies across sessions. Fixing it needs stable identity for serial-less bodies (the fleet has none today) or a refusal when two same-model bodies are attached; a design decision.

findings.description: vendor_target_serial touches the bus (usb_camera_list) before PtpUsbSession::open takes the CameraLock
findings.disposition_reason: Read-only descriptor reads; moving the lock earlier changes the open path and needs a hardware check.

findings.description: A failed language or serial descriptor read falls back to usb-<bus>:<addr>, so --serial <real> reports SerialNotFound for a present body (warning only on stderr)
findings.disposition_reason: Safe (refuses); the GUI hides stderr on failure. Needs the error to carry the warnings.

scope: issue filed for the one deferred High of nikon-fleet-20261028-e5a3

findings.description: The FTP-profile write cannot be self-verified: slot 0 is hard-coded (every write overwrites it), the 82-byte block is copied from one capture and contains a MAC-shaped value and bytes that decode to 192.168.66.87, the original test rig's Z 9 address, shipped to every camera; limits are guesses; no read-back; `RESP_OK` is trusted as proof. The 331-byte capture variant is not modelled.
findings.disposition_reason: Blocked on there being no known read operation for FTP profiles, so a write cannot be verified; with one, the address-block, slot, field-limit and 331-byte-variant questions become write/read-back experiments on a body. Partly addressed in 9da8a99 (block decoded, network tail parameterised, RESP_OK documented as the only ack, indeterminate failure typed). Tracked in https://github.com/blwfish/nikon-fleet/issues/5.

test_stats: not applicable (ledger update)

scope: closing six light-review findings fixed earlier but never recorded, fixing the open Lows and Medium that were cheap (snapshot atomicity, firmware status, MCP exit path, vendor lock ordering, SerialNotFound), and checking ClockDateTime

findings.description: kill_and_reap has no timeout and runs while the queue lock is held, so a worker stuck in unkillable USB I/O wedges every later camera call
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-10-28 remediation (9da8a99), recorded late: the supervisor bounds the reap after a kill (5 s) with an injected future; a never-completing reap is tested at, below and above the limit.

findings.description: The snapshot filename embeds the raw USB serial: only the label is sanitised, so a device serial containing / or .. could redirect the write
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in 9da8a99, recorded late: Snapshot::suggested_filename sanitises model, serial and label, so a separator in a device serial cannot redirect the write.

findings.description: limit: 0 returns next: Some(offset), so a client following next loops
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in 9da8a99, recorded late: next is only set when asking for it would advance; limit 0 pinned at several offsets.

findings.description: A label starting with '-' is rejected by clap as an unknown flag
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in 9da8a99, recorded late: allow_hyphen_values on --label and --notes; binary test.

findings.description: One non-UTF-8 byte on the worker's result channel kills the worker
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in 9da8a99, recorded late: the supervisor reads the result channel as raw bytes (ChannelLines); an invalid line is counted as garbage and the read continues.

findings.description: The offline MCP tools have no deadline or cap
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in 9da8a99, recorded late: offline tools have a 30 s deadline (180 s for firmware_status) and fail with tool_deadline. No output-size cap was added; limit is already clamped to 500.

findings.description: Firmware status reports 'not archived' when the archive was unreadable, and a USB scan failure is dropped, so an MCP agent cannot tell no body attached from a failed scan
findings.disposition_reason: firmware_status uses scan_archives: unreadable entries are reported with error_kind, 'held' is null (unknown) rather than false when an entry could not be read, and each model carries the USB scan result (complete, enumeration_error, unreadable). The CLI's print_survey still prints the old status text (see the new finding).

findings.description: Snapshot saves are not atomic, so a truncated file is not counted toward the 200/50 caps
findings.disposition_reason: save_to_file uses write_atomic; save_new stages, fsyncs and publishes with hard_link (no clobber, refuses a symlink), falling back to a checked rename only where links are unsupported; a failure leaves neither file nor temp; retention ignores temp files.

findings.description: The server exit path can drop a half-finished apply
findings.disposition_reason: On stdin EOF after --exit-wait-secs, or on SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, a call that reached writing leaves <data-dir>/in-flight-apply.json, reported once as previous_session_incomplete in the next session's first structured result (then renamed .seen). A SIGKILL mid-apply is not covered by this design.

findings.description: ClockDateTime is not on the never-copy list, so a full restore or undo could reset the camera clock to the snapshot's time
findings.disposition_reason: Checked in the code: ClockDateTime (33060) decodes to {"_type":"datetime"}; restore reaches the write attempt but sdk::prepare_write has no data form for that shape, so it returns UnsupportedWrite before SetCapability and the step is unsupported_write_type; undo takes the same path; transplant skips the shape as unsupported_value_shape. Pinned by three tests (all kinds 0..=40, full/other-body/undo restores, transplant). Residual: a future body reporting the clock as a numeric or string kind would be written; no snapshot or doc shows that. Not verified on hardware.

findings.description: vendor_target_serial touches the bus (usb_camera_list) before PtpUsbSession::open takes the CameraLock
findings.disposition_reason: vendor-read and vendor-write-ftp take the CameraLock first and resolve an id-N serial inside it (PtpUsbSession::open_locked hands the held lock to the session, no second flock); ordering pinned by a test with a busy and a granted lock.

findings.description: A failed language or serial descriptor read falls back to usb-<bus>:<addr>, so --serial <real> reports SerialNotFound for a present body (warning only on stderr)
findings.disposition_reason: PtpUsbError::SerialNotFound carries the unreadable bodies as a typed field and its text says N attached body(ies) could not be read and the serial may be on one of them.

findings.description: FTP write ops (0x90E8 setup, 0x90EE profile write) remain TxidCheck::Unchecked
findings.disposition_reason: Left Unchecked on purpose: it was a hardware-evidence decision. Since 9da8a99 a mismatching reply is recorded and surfaced (FtpWriteReceipt.reply_matched_command, a CLI stderr note), so it is no longer silent. Closing it needs hardware captures showing that the camera's replies to 0x90E8 and 0x90EE always echo the transaction id, which would justify Enforce.

findings.description: A dry-run restore lists ClockDateTime as would_write while the real run reports unsupported_write_type
findings.disposition_reason: The plan promises a write the real run refuses by kind; harmless to the body but the plan is wrong. Fixing it means checking prepare_write's kind support in the planner.

findings.description: The CLI's print_survey (firmware latest / fetch) still prints 'NEW - not in archive' from the readable entries only and does not print usb_scan
findings.disposition_reason: Unreadable entries do appear as warning lines; the MCP firmware_status is correct. CLI wording only.

findings.description: An apply that completes after the client has gone, within the exit wait, loses its result, and a SIGKILL of the server mid-apply leaves no marker
findings.disposition_reason: The marker covers a half-finished apply at exit/signal; keeping the last Finished (or writing the marker when writing starts and removing it on completion) would cover these two at some cost to the other case. A design choice.

findings.description: A crash between staging and publishing a snapshot leaves a stray .<name>.<pid>.<n>.tmp that nothing cleans up
findings.disposition_reason: Ignored by listings and the caps; harmless but accumulates. A sweep on startup would need a rule for 'stale'.

findings.description: The termination-signal handler calls write(2) without saving and restoring errno
findings.disposition_reason: Standard practice is to preserve errno in a handler; the handler runs on the thread it interrupts. Practical risk is small (the process exits right after).

findings.description: MCP supervisor kills the worker 3 s after its result; the 10 s watchdog can neve — TEARDOWN_LIMIT (10 s, chosen above the 4.7 s + 0.3 s slow-but-finishing disconnect) lives in the lib, the supervisor grace (3 s) in mcp, and the GUI CAMERA_CLI_TIMEOUT (90 s, with a stale comment) in the gui: three unrelated constants. Under MCP the supervisor SIGKILLs the worker 3 s after the result, so the watchdog is dead code on that path and a slow-but-finishing disconnect is killed mid-disconnect, the case the 10 s limit was designed not to cut. The kill pre-dates this delta and costs only a retry of the exit, so the net effect is a diag event that never appears and a doc claim ('bounded at 10 s') that is false for MCP.

findings.description: Watchdog thread can die before _exit: eprintln! on a closed stderr panics, and d — The watchdog prints with eprintln! If stderr is a pipe whose reader is gone, the thread panics before _exit and the process hangs exactly as it did without the watchdog; a stuck diag write would delay _exit the same way. Also: a teardown finishing at the instant the timer fires may print 'Error:' twice, and a failure between connect and the first write still waits.

findings.description: vendor-read-ftp --raw 'masked' dump leaves real password bytes when it matches a — The mask zeroes only the FIRST occurrence (find_subslice) of the password and of ssid_5ghz anywhere in the raw blob, but profile name, SSIDs, host and username precede the password in the layout. A password equal to (or contained in) an earlier field, e.g. username 'nikon'/password 'nikon' or 5 GHz SSID equal to the 2.4 GHz SSID, gets that earlier copy zeroed and the real password printed in the hex dump the command calls masked. The decoder knows the exact offset but the code searches by content; the test uses distinct values only. Same defect class as ledger 7b2e#06 (dry-run hex leak), reintroduced on the read side.
