findings.description: Watchdog-cut hung DisconnectDevice is recorded 'ok' and clean exit, contradictin — disconnect_device is Class::Top; shutdown() closes open Top spans Ok for code 0 and Failed otherwise, and only Leaf spans become Abandoned. On a Z 9 write apply that prints applied_verified and then hangs in DisconnectDevice, the watchdog calls exit_now(0)->shutdown(0), so the report shows 'disconnect_device ok (10 s)' and 'exited cleanly (code 0)' - exactly the hang the facility exists to expose (F26 was found by this open span). docs/diagnostics.md:62,66 promise 'abandoned'; unit tests use a Leaf 'disconnect' span and the worker_cli watchdog test uses selftest with no disconnect span, so nothing catches it.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: GUI argv builders for discover/snapshot/check/firmware no longer run through the — The deleted tests/gui_cli_argv_parity.rs fed 12 builder shapes (discover, ls, firmware ls, snapshot, ref set, firmware add/browse, vendor-read, vendor-write-ftp...) to the real clap parser via NIKON_FLEET_PARSE_ONLY. The remaining parser tests cover only the shared builders (gui_argv::restore_argv/transplant_argv, vendor_argv). The egui builders for discover --json, snapshot (--serial=, --label=), check (--allow-partial) and firmware are checked only against hard-coded strings, and cli_apply_flags.rs checks flag existence against its own hand-written list. Renaming a CLI flag keeps every test green and the GUI fails at runtime with a clap usage error (exit 2).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: GUI hard-codes exit status 4 separately from the CLI's EXIT_WRITE_INDETERMINATE  — The GUI defines its own EXIT_FTP_WRITE_INDETERMINATE = 4 (the other statuses come from the lib) and its test fakes the CLI with a shell `exit 4`. exit_code_for now also maps PropWriteIndeterminate (vendor-set-string) to 4, but the GUI message at gui/src/main.rs:2457 still says an FTP profile cannot be read back. Nothing ties the two constants together, so a renumbering silently turns an 'indeterminate write, check the camera' into a plain failure that invites a blind retry; and the two copies already disagree on meaning.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: FTP write guidance is wrong: read-back slot, 'idempotent' retry, and the reorder — vendor-write-ftp-blob prints 'Wrote. Read it back with: vendor-read-ftp --slot N', but per the experiment docs a successful 0x90EE moves the written profile to the FRONT (replace at slot N>0 and add at COUNT land at slot 0), so that read shows a different old profile. The FtpWriteIndeterminate text (and exit-4 advice) says 'repeating the write is idempotent', which is false for an add (a retry after an indeterminate (count,1) adds a duplicate) and for slot>0 replaces (retry hits a different profile and reorders again). The plan says 'REPLACE the stored profile in that slot' without mentioning the reorder; the Python script documents the ordering rule but the Rust text does not.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: write_ftp_profile_blob(_locked) has no slot/param2 guard; the CLI's count check  — The library entry points forward slot and param2 unvalidated (only the model gate and decodability are checked). The only bound (slot > count) lives in cmd_vendor_write_ftp_blob, which reads the count in one CameraLock session and writes in a second, so a count change between them turns an 'add' into a write to an existing slot. --param2 accepts any u32 including 0xFFFFFFFF, a value the probe refuses because slot 0xFFFFFFFF hung the camera's network stack until power-cycled; the library docs say param2's meaning is 'partly unknown'.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. Library guard + in-session count (fb23f9c); CLI uses plan_ftp_write and the verified write (89dd419).

findings.description: vendor-probe-op sends destructive FTP ops (0x90EA delete-all, 0x90EF(n) delete)  — FTP_PROBE_OPS includes 0x90EA, which the 2026-07-10 session proved deletes ALL stored profiles, and 0x90EF(n), which deletes profile n. Unlike every other FTP-writing path (ftp_write_confirmed / --force-unconfirmed-model), probe_ftp_op(_locked) checks only the op list; an unsurveyed model yields just a warning. The command help still says 'What these ops do is unknown; one of them may delete a profile', understating a documented delete-everything op.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Teardown watchdog is armed by hand at three call sites; early-return and error e — arm_teardown_watchdog is called only after the result is printed, at restore_run, transplant_run and worker with_body. restore_run's `product.print(..)?` runs after a real apply but before arming; transplant_run's `after_apply(..)?` (refusal, e.g. stale plan exit 5, which happens before any write) and `json_out.emit(..)?` (after the write) return without arming; worker `fail!` returns and with_body early returns after connect (ensure_capabilities, judge refusal, save failure) fall to Device::drop with an unbounded DisconnectDevice. Example: a GUI transplant with a stale --expect-digest exits 5, but if DisconnectDevice hangs (about 1 run in 14, F24) the GUI sees TimedOut instead of PlanStale. exit_now(0) is likewise scattered per site with no command classification.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: MCP supervisor kills the worker 3 s after its result; the 10 s watchdog can neve — TEARDOWN_LIMIT (10 s, chosen above the 4.7 s + 0.3 s slow-but-finishing disconnect) lives in the lib, the supervisor grace (3 s) in mcp, and the GUI CAMERA_CLI_TIMEOUT (90 s, with a stale comment) in the gui: three unrelated constants. Under MCP the supervisor SIGKILLs the worker 3 s after the result, so the watchdog is dead code on that path and a slow-but-finishing disconnect is killed mid-disconnect, the case the 10 s limit was designed not to cut. The kill pre-dates this delta and costs only a retry of the exit, so the net effect is a diag event that never appears and a doc claim ('bounded at 10 s') that is false for MCP.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Watchdog thread can die before _exit: eprintln! on a closed stderr panics, and d — The watchdog prints with eprintln! (which panics on EPIPE; SIGPIPE is ignored in Rust) and records a diag event (state mutex + file I/O) before calling exit_now. If stderr is a pipe whose reader is gone, the thread panics before _exit and the process hangs exactly as it did without the watchdog; a stuck diag write would delay _exit the same way. Also: a teardown finishing at the instant the timer fires may print 'Error:' twice, and a failure between connect and the first write still waits.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. Fixed except two sub-items: the double 'Error:' print race needs a hook in main(); a failure between connect and first write still waits (design decision).

findings.description: vendor-write-ftp --port is echoed as the FTP port but written to the second port — FtpProfile.port is written to the u16 after the password (8080 in every camera blob); the FTP port the camera uses is the u16 before the username, hard-coded 21 by the encoder. `--port 2121` is silently ignored and the success line prints user@host:2121; the default 21 also writes 21 where cameras carry 8080. The struct doc already says 'probably not the FTP server port'; the CLI help and success line do not. (Command pre-dates the delta; the docs that expose it are new.)
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. Help and the success line now say it is the second port (8080 in every camera blob) and that FTP port 21 is fixed by the encoder; the DEFAULT value is unchanged (changing the bytes written needs a hardware run).

findings.description: vendor-write-ftp-blob plans 'ADD (untested)' for slot==count with default --para — The 2026-11-05 Z 9 experiment sent 0x90EE(1,0) at count 1: data sent, USB pipe stall, nothing added; only (count,1) adds (the Python script requires --allow-create for it). The Rust command prints 'Would ADD' for any slot==count regardless of param2 and does not refuse (count,0) up front, so following the plan lands in FtpWriteIndeterminate/exit 4 with a pipe stall; the dry run also skips the model gate so it previews a write the Z 5 refuses. Help still calls the add 'untested'.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. The plan says ADD/REPLACE and 'front'; the default --param2 stays 0, so an add is --slot COUNT --param2 1 (the 2026-11-05 Z 9 experiment: (count,0) stalls and stores nothing).

findings.description: vendor-set-string --dry-run validates less than the real write; no CLI test for  — The dry run refuses only an unknown property code, then prints 'Would write... Nothing was sent.' It skips non-Latin-1 text, control characters (PropValueBad), the STRING_PROP_WRITE_MODELS gate and the descriptor read-write check that the real write enforces, contradicting the comment that a dry run must not suggest a change that cannot be made. The FTP command has a test (the_dry_run_preview_fails_exactly_where_the_real_write_fails); this one has none and no CLI test exists for vendor-set-string at all (precedents 7b2e#06, e5a3#55, e5a3#72).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: vendor-set-string: write accepted but read-back differs/unreadable exits 1, not  — SetDevicePropValue accepted and then the read-back differs or cannot be read: the command bails with a plain failure (exit 1, span Failed), though the camera has definitely or possibly changed. Exit 4 is reserved for PropWriteIndeterminate before an OK reply, and the command re-implements the indeterminate mapping inline instead of using vendor_write_error. By the repo's contract 1 is blind-retryable while unknown effect is 4; VendorSetStringArgs has no after_help documenting exit 4.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Two hand-typed write allow-lists with different meanings; the string gate admits — STRING_PROP_WRITE_MODELS (Z 9, Z6_3, Z 5) is a model-level gate whose own doc says only the image comment (0xD090) was confirmed; Artist/Copyright (0xD072/0xD073) writes are 'not run on any model' yet pass with no force flag, the class of unconfirmed op the FTP gate exists to stop. FTP_WRITE_CONFIRMED_MODELS (Z 9, Z6_3) is a second list; the FTP list has a drift guard (every_write_confirmed_model_is_a_surveyed_model) but the string list's only test iterates the const itself, and neither has a firmware dimension (ledger e5a3#03, fixed once, same shape).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. Artist/Copyright need --force-unconfirmed-model and both lists have drift guards; the firmware dimension is not modelled (same shape as e5a3#03).

findings.description: vendor-probe-op: a lost reply after data-out is flattened to a string and the co — A probe with --data sends data-out to an op that may delete a profile; if the transaction then errors, the typed PtpUsbError is turned into Err(String) inside FtpOpProbe.reply/after, the command exits 0, the ptp span says Indeterminate but the CLI status and command span say Ok. Timeout, pipe stall and poisoned session are indistinguishable, and the result does not say whether the probed op was transmitted (setup failure and op failure land in the same string). txn_outcome also has a catch-all Err(_)=>Failed.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: vendor-probe-op before/after list cannot show most changes, and loops on a camer — FtpListState keeps only the decoded profile name or '(undecodable, N bytes)'; no raw bytes or hash, so a probe that changes the password, host or SSID of a profile (or an undecodable profile of the same length) reports an unchanged list, defeating the probe's stated purpose. ftp_list_state iterates 0..info.count (camera-supplied u32) with no cap against the limit, and undecodable entries are counted nowhere. FtpProfileInfo guid/header/trailer/device_name/limit are dropped from snapshots.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Probe argument validation copy-pasted (probe_ftp_op vs _locked) and the allowed- — The op/param/data-length checks (params<=2, no u32::MAX, data<=32 as bare magic numbers) are byte-identical in probe_ftp_op and probe_ftp_op_locked; the FtpProbeOpNotAllowed message and VendorProbeOp help hard-code the op list separately from FTP_PROBE_OPS. Today they agree; nothing enforces it, and the lock-less variant would be the one to rot.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Stale help/doc text contradicts shipped behaviour (FTP read 'not yet tried', no  — Help and errors still say vendor-read-ftp 'has not been run over USB' / 'Never run over USB before' and the exit-4 advice cites it, although reads work (handoff 2026-11-05); a module doc says no way to choose another slot while write_ftp_profile_blob takes one; FtpProfileInfo::count doc says 'meaning unknown, 3 on Z6III with none' though count = stored profiles and guards key on it; doc comments are attached to the wrong items (0x943B doc on TXN_PHASE_COMMAND_SENT, as_encodable doc on is_sftp).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Diagnostics prune keeps the 20 newest-mtime files and ignores whether the owner  — prune has no liveness check, so an idle long-lived GUI or MCP server loses its in-flight and ring files once 20 newer short-lived processes (every CLI call and every MCP worker writes its own pair) have run; the live process then appends to an unlinked ring inode and its history is gone from the report. Tests cover only KEEP+5, not KEEP-1/KEEP/KEEP+1 or a live process. (Verified by the orchestrator.)
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Reused pid makes a leftover in-flight file read as 'still running with spans ope — Diag::new truncates the new process's ring but leaves a stale inflight-<pid>.json from an earlier killed process with the same pid, and verdict() decides liveness with kill(pid,0) alone; InflightFile.process_started_ms is written but never compared. A recycled pid therefore shows another process's spans as the live process's hung state, or a dead process as running; a missing/mistyped exit code is also rendered 'exited cleanly (code 0)' via unwrap_or(0).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: verdict() ignores read problems: unparseable data reads as 'exited cleanly' or ' — An unparseable inflight file yields inflight=None, so the verdict says 'killed between operations' or 'exited cleanly', contradicting the separate problem line; only the last problem is kept (later overwrites earlier); an exit/start record is matched on op string alone without subsystem; an older/newer-format inflight file fails whole and the process's open spans disappear.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Diagnostics file formats are unversioned with closed enums: one unknown value dr — Subsystem/Outcome/Class/Kind/Val and InflightFile.role are closed serde enums with no schema/version field, no unknown fallback and no deny_unknown_fields counter. A file from another build with one new value fails the entry (or the entire inflight file, losing all that process's open spans) and is reported as a 'line cut off by a kill', which is wrong for this cause.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: GUI quit closes open command spans as Ok and exit code 0 while the child may sti — on_exit calls shutdown(0), which closes every open Class::Top span (cli_child for a write apply, gui_cmd) as Ok; the camera child may still be running and later worker-thread spans are recorded after the exit event.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Spans are judged Ok regardless of failures inside (execute_writes, capture_reads — execute_writes ends Outcome::Ok with only a step count even if every step was WriteFailed (docs list written/write_errors for it but the code records neither); capture_reads is Ok even if every read failed; the gui_cmd span ends Ok for any Planned/Applied event though Applied can carry Indeterminate or NotApplied. Failure is visible only as counts or in the inner span.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: shutdown races and spans begun after shutdown rewrite the in-flight file, so a c — exited.swap(true) happens before shutdown writes, so a concurrent second caller (watchdog vs main) returns immediately and the watchdog's _exit can precede the winner's exit entry / inflight removal. A GUI worker thread or any thread outliving exit_now can begin spans after shutdown, rewriting inflight-<pid>.json, and verdict ranks open spans above the recorded exit (clean exit shown as 'gone, spans still open'). end()/set_field silently no-op when the seq is gone, with no counter.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Panic hook can deadlock on the diag mutex and stores panic message text — The hook calls d.event(), which takes the non-reentrant state mutex before unwinding; a panic on a thread already holding it hangs instead of aborting. A concrete chain: note_write's eprintln! runs while the lock is held and panics on a closed stderr pipe, then the hook re-locks. The hook also records the panic message via Val::text (unwrap on Err(Debug) can carry argv/URL/payload text), against 'never record error text that can embed these'.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Diagnostics write failures are not surfaced: counter never reported, compaction  — Diag::write_failures is read only by tests, though the module doc and docs/diagnostics.md say it appears in the report and is 'warned once' (code warns once per streak). compact() can rename the new file then fail to reopen, keeping a handle on the unlinked inode so later writes 'succeed', clear the streak and are lost; a failed write_inflight leaves a stale inflight file with ended spans, giving a false 'hung' verdict; a second write error (trace file) is discarded by first-error-wins; the compact error branch is untested and its comment is wrong.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. Fixed; the stale-file removal on a failed inflight write and a real reopen failure are not covered by a test.

findings.description: Boundary and vacuity gaps in the new diagnostics/watchdog tests — prune is tested at KEEP+5 only (no KEEP-1/KEEP/KEEP+1, no live process); render last_n and age_text 999/1000 ms, the verdict (exit event + spans open) arm, and the compact error branch are untested; TEARDOWN_LIMIT's test asserts only 8..30 s, not the relation to the 5.0 s slow-but-finishing case; tests/worker_cli.rs a_refused_camera_lock... returns silently when sdk-runtime/MaidLayer.config is absent and so passes vacuously.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: reset_nikon_usb_cameras result and per-device failures dropped; usb_reset span f — reset_nikon_usb_cameras returns the number of successful resets, which is discarded; open failures are skipped and reset().is_ok() is thrown away, so the usb_reset span records Ok with no fields even if no camera was reset (unchecked-result rule).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: SDK error detail never reaches the spans: Span::done drops Err text and read/wri — Sdk::open/initialize_sdk use span.done(&result), which discards the error, so SdkCall{call,code}, Load{path,source}, Symbol(name) and the InitializeSDK return code never reach the report; read_cap/write_cap hand-roll a finish match with the code only inside the Display string while connect/devices record a typed Val::I64 code. Hand-rolled finish matches repeat in 5 places.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. Fixed in sdk.rs (a2), ptp_usb.rs (tag/diag_fields, d50ca27) and the MCP supervisor (aeb430c).

findings.description: Identical single-line apply span-judge closure duplicated in apply.rs and restor — The same ~300-character closure (status.diag_outcome(), status/written/write_errors/no_op fields) is pasted in both files; a field added to one copy silently diverges the two records for what the docs table treats as one span.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: 'model not in KNOWN_MODELS' warning block pasted 5 times, with text that no long — The five blocks say the operation 'was only captured on a Z 9' while the condition is KNOWN_MODELS membership (which includes Z6III and Z 5); one shared helper would carry one message.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Repeated PTP step sequences in ptp_usb: require_ok+NoDataPhase x7, ftp_list_stat — The require_ok + NoDataPhase pair, the 0x90E8/0x90EB/0x90ED sequence (once in read_ftp_profile_slot, again in ftp_list_state) and the 0x90E8 setup transaction are re-written in write/read/list/probe, alongside a test-only read_ftp_profile wrapper and six *_locked shims.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. The require_ok+NoDataPhase pairs and the 0x90E8/0x90EB/0x90ED sequence now go through shared helpers; the six *_locked shims remain (public API, three-line wrappers, no drift risk).

findings.description: Three PTP-string decoders and two encoders with different strictness — FtpBlobReader::ptp_string is a near-copy of DeviceInfoReader::string (anomalies become FtpBlobMalformed in one, stay on the Ok value in the other), decode_ptp_string_value is a third strict decoder used for set-string read-back, and utf16_u8_len_bytes/encode_ptp_string_value a second encoder. The differences look deliberate (strict for writes, lenient for DeviceInfo) but are documented nowhere and pinned by no cross-decoder test; they have already diverged in behaviour.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: main.rs vendor command boilerplate: vendor_locked_target closure ~10x, STRING_PR — Each vendor command repeats the vendor_locked_target + lock + map_err preamble, the STRING_PROPS lookup/allowed-list is duplicated with set_string_property, and ftp_probe_text/vendor_op_query_text re-compose the data-phase description.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. The lock+resolve preamble is one helper in 9 commands; the ftp_probe_text/vendor_op_query_text overlap was reduced by the deviation-note helper.

findings.description: parse_u32_any hand-copied twin of ptp_usb::parse_propcode — parse_propcode's doc says it is shared so the accepted input format cannot drift; parse_u32_any in main.rs re-implements the same decimal/0x-hex parse for u32 with different wording and no shared core.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: macOS fallback menu bar omits Preferences, About and Quit when the native bar fa — ui_menu_bar renders menus(MACOS) even in the fallback path, and menus(true) leaves out Edit/Help and moves Settings/About/Quit into the native application menu. When NativeMenu::install fails (the notice says 'the menus are in the window instead') those three actions have no in-window entry, and the toolbar buttons for Preferences/Vendor Ops/Transplant were removed in this diff. The test every_action_is_in_exactly_one_place counts MAC_APP_MENU as a place, so it passes.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Native macOS app menu is hand-written separately from MAC_APP_MENU; the guard is — NativeMenu::install builds the Fleet menu items by hand while MAC_APP_MENU is the declared list; the debug_assert checks only Preferences and Quit (not About) and is absent in release builds, contradicting the module doc's single-source claim.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Python probe's write gate is weaker than the Rust decoder; setup rc ignored; rea — In --write --send mode the 0x90E8 setup return code is discarded (rc,_,_ = step) and 0x90EB's rc unchecked, then 0x90EB and 0x90EE are sent, though the Rust docs say a write hangs without a successful setup. decode_profile lacks the padding/IPv6/trailer/trailing-bytes checks of decode_ftp_profile (a truncated or garbage-suffixed blob passes the 'decodes' gate), declared lengths are unbounded, and the read path sends 0x90ED(slot) with no slot<count check although the docstring warns slot 0xFFFFFFFF hung the camera network until power-cycled.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Python probe --out saves the raw profile blob (with FTP password) with default u — open(a.out,'wb').write(blob) creates the file 0644 under the default umask, never closes it, overwrites an existing file, and runs after decode so a decode exception loses the blob. The Rust --save-blob uses create_new with 0600. The docstring says keep the file private, but the script does not.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: FTP blob decoder rejects any non-ASCII SSID/username/password (ascii_u32_len) — SSIDs are arbitrary octets in 802.11 and Japanese-market bodies commonly see non-ASCII names; the decoder returns FtpBlobMalformed for the whole profile, with no raw fallback, so vendor-read-ftp shows 'not decoded' and vendor-write-ftp-blob refuses to copy that profile.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. u32-length text is read as UTF-8 by analogy with IPTC (no capture has non-ASCII); non-UTF-8 octets stay an error naming the field. Encoder stays ASCII-only. Hardware-unverified assumption.

findings.description: Typed results of the vendor reads drop observations the experiments need — VendorOpQuery drops reply.params, deviation detail and unrecognized_containers (for 0x944C the reply is the finding); FtpProfileReadout and FtpProbeReply drop response params from 0x90E8/0x90EB/0x90ED and collapse ReplyDeviation{got} to a bool; get_device_prop drops params; a malformed 0x90EB discards the raw info bytes.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: ingest_bundle commits firmware.bin before the source-page sidecar write; a sidec — After rename(part -> firmware.bin) the code does fs::write(source-page.html)? and only then writes metadata.json; if the sidecar write fails (disk full, permission) the function returns an error with firmware.bin committed and no metadata.json, and every later ingest of that version fails with IncompleteArchive until someone removes it by hand. Writing the sidecar before the rename, or best-effort, avoids it.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: data_hash/reply_hash of the 0x90EE/0x90ED blob (password inside) is a 64-bit SHA — The USB layer hashes the whole ~325-byte profile blob (mostly known structure plus a low-entropy password) and stores the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 in the diagnostics files; the docs say payload bytes are never recorded and only length and hash reach a file, which is literally true but lets someone with the file test password guesses offline. The comment 'never' overclaims; the panic hook's message text is covered separately.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Error text from SDK/USB/supervisor errors is recorded though docs say error text — e.to_string() for SDK, USB and supervisor errors is stored as Val::text at about five sites with nothing enforcing that the Display never embeds a payload, path or URL; today the Displays carry codes and names only.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Diag dir hygiene: chmod 0700 on a pre-existing NIKON_FLEET_DIAG_DIR, and orphan  — private_dir sets 0700 even on an existing user-supplied directory (and makes Diag::new fail, so diagnostics off, when the user is not the owner); write_private_atomic's temp files (.inflight-<pid>.json.<pid>.<n>.tmp) are not matched by pid_of_file_name, so a process killed between create and rename leaves a file that prune and load never see.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Ring reader fails the whole file on one invalid UTF-8 byte; unbuffered writeln i — fs::read_to_string on the ring file reports zero entries and a read problem if a line is cut mid-character (entries contain non-ASCII, e.g. the truncation mark and camera strings), against the docs' 'cut last line is expected and counted malformed'. writeln! on the unbuffered File is two write syscalls per entry, so a shared --trace FILE written by several processes can fuse lines that are then counted malformed.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: process_exit/exit-status housekeeping: stale module doc, non-unix exit path, Err — The module header still says exit_now is only for commands that wrote nothing while the watchdog calls it on write paths; the cfg(not(unix)) branch uses process::exit, which runs atexit handlers contrary to the doc; the design keeps ordinary disconnect for writes yet _exit's after 10 s anyway; 'Error: {e:?}' plus exit_code_for is composed in four places, transplant_exit_status/keeps_its_own_status mirror transplant_exit (one equality test holds them), and a wrapper builds an anyhow! just to compute the constant 1.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: MCP run() Err path now calls process::exit(1), skipping runtime drop and kill_on — Previously returning Err from #[tokio::main] dropped the runtime and killed in-flight workers; now the explicit exit leaves a worker running (holding the camera lock) and does not call record_in_flight_at_exit. Only reachable if service.waiting() returns a join error while a call is in flight.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: read_ftp_profile_slot(None) sends 0x90ED(info.slot) with no slot<count check — The explicit-slot branch refuses n >= count because 0x90ED(count) stalls the pipe, but the default branch sends 0x90ED(info.slot) whenever slot != 0xff; with count 0 and slot 0 it hits the same stall (recovered by clear_halt).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: FtpProfile::as_encodable ignores timestamps/camera_network/ipv6 and structural b — as_encodable returns Some without comparing timestamps, ipv6_fields or camera_network to the encoder's placeholders, so a decoded profile 'encodable' by the doc list silently changes on re-encode; the decoder checks header/tag/pad/trailer bytes and ssid24_lead (closed set {03,00}) then discards them, rejecting a whole profile on any deviation with no unknown-structure flag (the 331-byte variant of ledger e5a3#86 is the live example).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: DecodedFtpProfile, FtpProfileBlob and FtpProfileReadout derive Debug with the pl — Any {:?} of these types (or an anyhow chain holding one) prints the FTP password and the 5 GHz field; no production site does today.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: SDK diag fields: read_cap records nothing on success, write_cap no code, empty s — read_cap success records no fields and unknown types finish Ok; GetCapability data_type is not recorded; write_capability records no SDK code on success; serde_json::to_vec(..).unwrap_or_default() makes a failed serialization hash the empty buffer, which looks like a genuine value_hash; file_name().unwrap_or_default() yields an empty bundle name.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Disconnect workarounds: pump result discarded, code<0 re-encoded instead of chec — CFRunLoopRunInMode's return is discarded, so a pump that returns immediately makes the 300 ms wait a no-op with nothing recorded; the disconnect span re-encodes code<0 instead of using check() (sdk.rs:336); PRE_DISCONNECT_PUMP (300 ms) is tuned on small samples next to the watchdog, two workarounds for the same defect.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Python probe docstring still says 'read-only / nothing is written' though it has — The docstring's first line and its sentence 'Nothing is written to the camera' contradict the --write FILE --send mode (0x90EE) documented further up; the `port` it prints is the FTP port while the Rust encoder's `port` is the second port, inviting a wrong write-back; AGENT-README.md:56 omits the script from its scripts/ list; docs/diagnostics.md says the script 'writes nothing here' (diag).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Python probe protocol hygiene: unchecked lengths and txids, lossy decode, exit 0 — recv_pkt does not check ln >= 8 (negative count, stream desync); data-phase packets and the reply txid are not compared to the request; errors='replace' decoding with unbounded declared lengths ('*'*n allocation up to ~4 GiB); a write the camera does not accept prints 'NOT accepted' and exits 0, as does 'no profile data returned'; ssid24 lead/kind, GUID, device name and the selected-slot field are not shown.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Docs drift: exit status 4 documented for vendor-write-ftp only; worker status 2  — VENDOR_WRITE_HELP and EXIT_WRITE_INDETERMINATE name only vendor-write-ftp although vendor-write-ftp-blob and vendor-set-string can exit 4 and have no Exit-status help (tests/followup_vendor_exit_cli.rs covers only write-ftp and vendor-read); worker_cmd's header says status 2 means the result channel could not be established but 2 is also returned when the result line could not be written; sdk.rs:1861 and docs still mention the Python/tkinter GUI.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass. Exit status 4 documented for all three camera writes; worker header and tkinter mention fixed.

findings.description: The password-mask bug in `vendor-read-ftp --raw` was reproduced by execution in a scratch copy: the password stays in the default masked dump for username==password, password as a substring of the username, and password as a substring of the 2.4 GHz SSID. The existing test uses four mutually distinct values, so it cannot see this (same defect as code finding #1).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: STRING_PROP_WRITE_MODELS (the write gate for vendor-set-string) has no literal-contents test and no KNOWN_MODELS drift guard (its FTP sibling has both). Survivors: dropping "Z 5", and renaming "Z6_3" to "Z6III" (silently locks out the real Z6III); adding "Z 7" would also survive. The test iterates the const so it adapts to any edit.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: FTP_PROBE_OPS (allow-list of bare ops sent to the camera) is pinned only by refusing 0x90EE/0x90ED; replacing 0x90EA with 0x1016 (SetDevicePropValue) survived the whole ptp_usb suite. 0x90EA is never exercised.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: The PropWriteIndeterminate arm of exit_code_for can be deleted and every bin test passes: the only 'indeterminate gives 4' test uses the FTP variant, and the transplant test compares exit_code_for with itself. vendor-set-string returning 4 vs 1 is unpinned.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Watchdog glue (which status/error line is passed to bound_apply_teardown) is unpinned: flipping `!*report_in_hand` survived all 140 bin tests. The helper and the mechanism are well pinned (worker selftest path; 3 mutants killed), the glue needs an SDK and camera. Exposure is high (F26: 10 of 20 Z 9 write applies reach the watchdog).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: ApplyStatus::diag_outcome: all three mutants (Indeterminate to Ok, Failed to Ok, AppliedVerified to Failed) survived the 1,314-test lib suite. The diagnostic outcome of a write is asserted nowhere.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Probe limits are tested one-sided (params 3 and 1, not 2; data 33 and 2, not 32); `>` to `>=` survives for both. probe_ftp_op_locked, the only function main.rs calls, has zero tests: 32 to 320 survived.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: set_string_property's `Err(e) if self.data_phase_started` guard can become `if true` with all 260 ptp_usb tests passing; the FTP twin has a 'never got its data out is not indeterminate' test.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: FtpBlobReader::ptp_string / ascii_u32_len strictness is unpinned: embedded NUL, unpaired surrogate, missing terminator and non-ASCII rejection each survive when disabled, although write_ftp_profile_blob relies on decode_ftp_profile so that a garbled blob never reaches the camera. Anomalies are pinned only in the third decoder (decode_ptp_string_value).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: GUI argv builders (discover, snapshot, check, six firmware shapes) are pinned only as string literals and never fed to the real clap parser; the deleted parity tests did that for the Python GUI. GUI DiscoveredJson is tested against hand-written JSON, not the real serialization (see code finding #3).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: No test ties the Python decoder to the Rust one; the script's --write has no model gate or strict decode and its read has no slot<count guard.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: The inline write-safety gate `args.slot > count` in cmd_vendor_write_ftp_blob is untested; `>` to `>=` survived.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: parse_hex_bytes / parse_u32_any have 0 tests; odd-length acceptance and hex-parsed-as-decimal both survive. The lib re-validates length and 0xFFFFFFFF, so exposure is low.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Report formatting thresholds unpinned (age_text 999/1000/1001 ms, singular 'entry', 'unreadable line(s)' at 0, last_n equal/over): 5 survivors, text-only.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: An exit event with no `code` reads as ExitedCleanly(0) (`unwrap_or(0)`); changing the default survives. 1 site.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: pid_alive EPERM => Some(true) is unpinned (platform-specific).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Descriptor of exactly 5 bytes: `< 5` to `<= 5` survives (4 and 12 bytes are pinned).
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: as_encodable's `ftp_port == 21` and `folder.is_empty()` conjuncts are individually unpinned; 0 non-test callers, so exposure is nil today.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Latin-1 guard pinned at U+00FF/U+0100, but `char::is_control` also rejects U+0080..U+009F inside the admitted range; no test says so.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: A dry-run restore lists ClockDateTime as would_write while the real run reports unsupported_write_type
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: The termination-signal handler calls write(2) without saving and restoring errno
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in the 2026-11-05 remediation pass.

findings.description: Entry-point choreography and exit-to-outcome mapping repeated across CLI/MCP/GUI — diag start/span/finish/shutdown boilerplate is repeated in main, mcp main, gui main and worker_cmd, and only the CLI maps EXIT_WRITE_INDETERMINATE to Outcome::Indeterminate; the exit_now/watchdog route ends the span via shutdown, which marks any nonzero code Failed, so the same status is classified differently by route. Unreachable for 4 today (watchdog statuses are 0/1/5/6).
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Exit-to-outcome mapping is one function (exit_status::diag_outcome_for_exit). The start/span/finish/shutdown choreography is still repeated in the CLI, MCP, GUI and worker entry points; extracting it touches four entry points that each need their own unwinding and exit semantics. Needs its own change with the real-binary tests as the safety net.

findings.description: FTP profile layout is ad hoc byte compares; any decodable blob is sent with [slo — The write path accepts any blob the strict decoder accepts and forwards both parameters whose meaning is 'partly unknown'; on a Z 9 [0,0] replaced the only stored profile instead of adding one. There is no typed layout spec to generate encoder, decoder and gate from, so each new variant (e5a3#86's 331-byte form) needs three hand edits.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The unsafe forwarding of unknown params is closed by the #06 guard. The typed layout spec that generates encoder, decoder and gate is a large refactor of a byte-exact encoder that cannot be hardware-checked here; do it with a golden-vector test per field before touching the encoder.

findings.description: Ring eviction order contradicts its comment: successful USB vendor writes are ev — sdk.rs says Top spans mean writes are the last thing the ring evicts, but a successful Top span ranks 1 (below events and failed Leaf at 2); ptp_usb begin_txn_span makes every USB transaction a Leaf, so vendor writes (ptp_90ee, ptp_1016) have the lowest eviction rank 0 on success, and the sdk.rs:792 'keeps every failure' comment is false because a Leaf failure is evicted before a Top failure.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The eviction rank is as docs/diagnostics.md says; what is wrong are the comments at sdk.rs (~792, ~881) and the Leaf class of USB writes in ptp_usb.rs. A comment-and-class change in files other clusters were editing; trivial but not done.

findings.description: Ring eviction and text truncation are unmarked: no evicted counter, in-band trun — The report says 'last N of M' as if M were the whole history though older entries were evicted without a counter; truncated text carries only an in-band marker (no flag or original length), ambiguous with real text ending in it.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Eviction is now counted and reported; truncated text still only has the in-band mark. A typed 'truncated' marker changes the diagnostics file format.

findings.description: Report/reader fidelity details: ordering, aggregated runs, wall-clock durations, — load() iterates a BTreeSet<u32> so order is numeric pid, not 'oldest first' as documented; aggregated runs show only the first member's seq and fields with summed duration (the member nearest a hang is dropped); render omits timestamp/thread/class/depth for completed entries; durations for shutdown-closed spans use wall-clock unix_ms; duplicate keys set at begin and finish shadow each other; read.flatten() drops dirent errors; a non-UTF-8 request id is dropped; the Cancelled-outcome doc and the MCP server comment disagree; the docs state table lists 4 outcomes for 6 verdicts and omits the capture_reads span.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Processes are sorted by start time and the docs rows are fixed. Left: first-member-of-run seq, completed-entry columns, wall-clock durations for shutdown-closed spans, duplicate keys, dirent errors.

findings.description: Test isolation: 'test runs never touch the real diag dir' holds only under cargo — The NIKON_FLEET_DIAG_DIR override is applied only when cargo discovers .cargo/config.toml from the cwd (test binaries run directly, cargo invoked outside the tree, or CARGO_TARGET_DIR set make the relative path wrong), so spawned CLI/worker tests write into the real directory and count toward prune's 20-process window. The diag global().is_none() test and the GUI request-id tests share a process-wide OnceLock and a 1024-entry ring that other tests also fill.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Partly false-positive: the CARGO_TARGET_DIR claim is wrong (relative = true resolves against the config's parent) and the GUI side is isolated. Left: root integration tests and the global().is_none() test depend on cargo finding .cargo/config.toml; each spawn there should set NIKON_FLEET_DIAG_DIR to a tempdir.

findings.description: Efficiency: every span begin/end rewrites the whole in-flight file under the glo — Each span begin/end/set does tmp+write+close+rename of the in-flight file (about 10 syscalls per SDK read, 14 per USB transaction, 3 rewrites per transaction counting set('phase') twice) with a deep clone of the open list; push does an O(cap) min_by_key eviction scan and VecDeque::remove once full; compaction re-serializes all 1024 entries (~200 KB) under the lock every cap entries. A 200-read capture is about 2000 serialized syscalls.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Coalescing in-flight file rewrites weakens the write-ahead guarantee; it needs its own design and a measured cost first.

findings.description: Efficiency: hashing done even with diag off; span file I/O on the tokio/GUI thre — transact_within builds an extra Vec and SHA-256 of every reply and write_capability serde-serializes and hashes the value before the span even when diagnostics are off; supervisor span.set and GUI event handling do synchronous file I/O on the async executor / UI thread; every CLI invocation, including offline reads, runs create_dir_all, chmod and a prune read_dir with about 40 stats.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Needs batching or off-thread file writes in diag.rs, and the cost has not been measured. Hash-with-diag-off part not done.

findings.description: diag.rs simplification: unused enum variants and ALL tables, duplicated Entry/Op — Subsystem::PtpIp/Settings are never constructed; Subsystem::ALL/Outcome::ALL exist for tests only (a second copy of the names); Entry and OpenSpan duplicate 7 fields; span() and event() are copy-pasted; Span.finished shadows the diag Option; all 12 scoped callers ignore the &Span argument; install_panic_hook, OP_PANIC, DEFAULT_RING_CAP and KEEP_PROCESSES are needlessly pub; verdict/load/render nest deeply.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Removing enum variants or ALL tables changes the serde vocabulary of the diagnostics files; do it together with a schema bump.

findings.description: Small duplications: --save-blob 0600 open vs diag private_open, scoped_with vs d — The 0600 create_new open duplicates diag.rs private_open; firmware_source's scoped_with with an Ok/Failed judge equals diag::scoped; the GUI records stdin/stdout/stderr lengths as Val::U64 where the rest use Val::len (tests pin U64); worker_cmd note_phase repeats code.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Partly false-positive (the worker's note_phase is already one function; the firmware judge is now the rich fetch_span_result). Left: the --save-blob 0600 open duplicates diag's private_open.

findings.description: FTP_SSID_MAX_BYTES=32 is applied to the 5 GHz field, which the docs treat as pro — A value read by vendor-read-ftp that is longer than 32 bytes is refused by vendor-write-ftp with FtpFieldTooLong even though the raw-blob path (strict decoder only) accepts it.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Raising the 5 GHz limit beyond 32 sends an unprobed length to hardware; needs a write-at-limit experiment on a body.

findings.description: Event containers are skipped uncounted and a misaligned response discards collec — CONTAINER_EVENT => continue discards event containers with no counter (unrecognized kinds are counted); decode_response_params(..)? on a misaligned response drops the data-in already collected, which for 0x944C and the probe is the observation.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Event containers are now counted per session (event_container_count). A misaligned response still discards the collected data: the error type must carry the partial reply.

findings.description: ptp_string anomalies are always empty on Ok; descriptor PropCode echo is not com — ptp_string returns Err for any anomaly, so PtpString.anomalies on the Ok path is always empty and contradicts the StringAnomaly docs; set_string_property does not compare the 0x1014 descriptor's echoed PropCode, ignores the default string and form flag, and FtpProfileInfo.limit is extracted but unused.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The descriptor PropCode echo is now checked and the anomalies doc is corrected. Still ignored: the descriptor's default string and form flag, and FtpProfileInfo.limit (semantics unknown).

findings.description: SDK enumeration and array reads fail soft: unreadable descriptors, zero-device r — A device whose descriptor read fails is silently dropped from the camera list (contradicting the usb_camera_scan doc) and usb_scan Failed omits the enumeration error; devices() records Ok devices:0 after ten empty attempts with no per-device fields; a failed second GET_ARRAY call returns Value::Array(vec![]) and read_cap finishes Ok; take_capabilities indexes p_cap_array.add(i) with no null check; from_utf8_lossy and placeholder JSON for unsupported types are silent.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: A device whose descriptor will not read is now reported unreadable and usb_scan records enumeration_error. Left: per-device fields in devices(), lossy from_utf8_lossy/cstr_to_string decoding, read_usb_string swallowing errors (empty serial).

findings.description: Firmware http spans: timeouts not recorded, HTTP status flattened, redirected ho — http_span's doc says it records the timeouts but records only the host; HTTP status becomes text 'HTTP {code}' with error_kind 'http' so 404, 503 and timeouts look alike; only the first request's host is recorded though ureq follows up to 5 redirects; 'not a URL' and 'no host' both give an empty host; the 'io' kind covers local disk I/O and the body size cap, so an oversize page looks like ordinary I/O failure.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Timeouts, url_ok and the HTTP status are now typed on the spans. Left: a redirected host and splitting body-size-cap errors from disk I/O (ureq gives no typed signal; would mean parsing its error text).

findings.description: Firmware fetch/ingest spans omit results: error variant, expected vs computed si — fetch_direct finishes Failed on any error without the FetchError variant or expected/got size and sha; Release.warnings, the gate description, latest() parse failures and the numeric download id are not recorded; ingest_bundle records no Archived/AlreadyPresent; fs::remove_file(&part) failures (pre-existing) leave a full-size .part unrecorded.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The fetch and ingest spans now carry the error kind and the disagreeing sizes/hashes. Left: the gate description (needs a typed field on Release), latest() failures (outside the fetch span), the numeric download id (exists only inside the URL).

findings.description: A refused-camera-lock test returns silently (vacuous pass) when the gitignored sdk-runtime/MaidLayer.config is absent (3 such skips in the file); two no-op `let _ =` statements; only 1 of 11 menu labels and the macOS accelerator mapping are pinned.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The GUI menu labels and accelerators are pinned and the three worker_cli lock tests no longer pass vacuously. Left: the same silent skip in mcp/tests/stdio.rs when the gitignored sdk-runtime/MaidLayer.config is absent.

findings.description: The FTP-profile write cannot be self-verified: slot 0 is hard-coded (every write overwrites it), the 82-byte block is copied from one capture and contains a MAC-shaped value and bytes that decode to 192.168.66.87, the original test rig's Z 9 address, shipped to every camera; limits are guesses; no read-back; `RESP_OK` is trusted as proof. The 331-byte capture variant is not modelled.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: UPDATE 2026-11-05 (remediation of b7d3): the recorded blocker ('no known read operation') no longer holds. The library now has write_ftp_profile_blob_verified(_locked) (read slot 0 back in the write's own session, compare field by field, check the count), fb23f9c, and vendor-write-ftp-blob uses it and exits 4 when the read-back does not confirm (89dd419). It stays open because (1) the in-session read-back has never run on a camera and relies on 'a successful 0x90EE moves the profile to slot 0 and an add raises the count by one' from Z 9 experiments (a Z6III that does not move it would report a false mismatch), and (2) the encoder path vendor-write-ftp still writes slot 0 with no read-back. Closing it needs one Z 9 and one Z6III run of vendor-write-ftp-blob with the read-back, then the same for the encoder path.

findings.description: The known-good set is whatever one capture read, measured only on one Z 9 and the Z6III in one state (the Z 9 B was never attached); a state-dependent capability could make a healthy capture fail the gate.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Not investigated in this pass. The known-good set is whatever one capture read, measured on one Z 9 and the Z6III in one state; closing it needs the second Z 9 (B) attached and captures in more than one camera state.

findings.description: `set_active_configuration(1)` error swallowed, configuration hard-coded, two `pkill -9` spawns on every open. Behaviour-sensitive; verify on hardware before changing.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Needs a hardware experiment (configuration 1, the two pkill spawns).

findings.description: The 331-byte 0x90EE variant (an extra optional UTF-16 field, port 56171) is not modelled; the "byte-for-byte" claim holds for two of three captures.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The decoder models the 331-byte form (folder string plus flag byte). The encoder cannot write a folder without a bench test of what the camera does with it.

findings.description: The interrupt IN endpoint is never opened, so PTP events (DevicePropChanged) never arrive and the Event arm is unreachable; unknown container kinds are skipped without a counter.
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Opening the interrupt IN endpoint needs hardware and a design for what to do with events.

findings.description: FTP write ops (0x90E8 setup, 0x90EE profile write) remain TxidCheck::Unchecked
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Still needs hardware captures showing the 0x90E8 and 0x90EE replies always echo the txid before switching them from Unchecked to Enforce.

findings.description: restore targets the snapshot's own serial, which can be an id-N or bare number (an SDK id of the current session); with two same-model bodies a restore can land on the wrong body, and a GUI snapshot resolves id-N in a second SDK session
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The no-flag half is done (c2f9d59). Left: an explicit --serial id-N (which the GUI always passes from its listing) resolving in a second SDK session when two same-model bodies are attached. Refusing it breaks the GUI's only way to address a body whose USB serial is unreadable; the fleet has no stable identity for such bodies. A decision about a flag users type.

findings.description: An apply that completes after the client has gone, within the exit wait, loses its result, and a SIGKILL of the server mid-apply leaves no marker
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Even the first half (an apply that finishes after the client left, inside the exit wait) needs a new ExitReason, a marker field and the agent-facing note in guidance.rs plus tests/fixtures/agent_notes_golden.json. The SIGKILL half needs a write-ahead marker whose lifecycle (it can overwrite a previous session's unacknowledged marker) needs a design decision.

findings.description: three parallel per-code policy tables
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The combined question is already one function (never_skip). The per-code policy record would touch range_policy.rs, ops/restore.rs and ops/readback.rs, and tests index NEVER_TRANSPLANT[0] and NEVER_TRANSLATED directly.

findings.description: grab bag of heuristics (alias table, starts_with Z, placeholder text, element types)
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Side::as_str replaced the hand-typed 'source'/'target' literals (f6ac342). The alias table, starts_with('Z') and placeholder text need a model registry that does not exist; SkipReason::EnumUndecodedBySdk.side is still &'static str because the GUI builds it with literals.

findings.description: static NOT_TRANSFERABLE list reported for every target
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Informational; a derived list needs capture statistics.

findings.description: small simplifications (TransplantOutcome invariants, tag duplication)
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: A TransplantOutcome constructor changes a public struct with public fields used across files; changing Display/tag() changes the output contract.

findings.description: unrestorable/unrestored naming; no output schemas
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Renaming unrestorable/unrestored changes the JSON clients see and there are no output schemas to update.

findings.description: no live kind check against the translated value's shape
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: A kind check on an opted-in number written onto an enum/range target needs a new skip variant, which changes plan JSON and text. Today it fails safe (LiteralUnconfirmed unless opted in, an SDK InvalidValue write failure if opted in). Owner decision on the output contract.

findings.description: datetime/array/unknown/null collapse into UnsupportedValueShape
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: Splitting UnsupportedValueShape needs new variants or a payload, which changes JSON shape and tags.

findings.description: truncation signalled only by an in-band marker
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: A typed 'truncated' field means a new field in the SkipReason JSON; only matters for unusually long text.

findings.description: imprecise skip attribution
findings.disposition_reason: Remediation pass 2026-11-05: The unrecognized live elem_type is now EnumUndecodedBySdk{side:target} instead of a bad snapshot (f6ac342). The other MalformedSource sites and the range shape mismatch reported as target_read_failed need new variants.

findings.description: numeric target read error discarded
findings.disposition_reason: The .ok() is deliberate and commented: the plan shows changes: null, and surfacing the error would change plan output.

findings.description: enum/range write data default absent fields
findings.disposition_reason: decode_value always emits every field; making enum_write_data/range_write_data strict would risk existing fixtures that build minimal JSON, and restore already refuses a stepped range with no usable position.

findings.description: CodeNameGuard default-allow when a section lacks the code
findings.disposition_reason: Documented on check and pinned by an existing test (check(1), check(2) and check(999) all return Ok).

findings.description: RangeClamped reported even when nothing was clamped
findings.disposition_reason: RangeClamped is the wire-format name; the Strategy doc says it is the identity on an equal scale. Renaming or splitting it changes the output contract.

findings.description: packed_string_options error swallowed in resolve_choice
findings.disposition_reason: Unreachable today: translate_enum has already run packed_string_options successfully on both sides; propagating the error would change the public resolve_choice signature and the None already fails safe.

findings.description: duplicate capability ids keep the last
findings.disposition_reason: The SDK capability list has unique ids; a duplicate would be a harness fault and no policy was chosen for it.

findings.description: On Tk 8.6 (python.org Python 3.13 and older) the Python/tk GUI tests hang: TestStartup::test_a_settings_error_is_shown_and_nothing_is_guessed never returns from Tk's `update` (the pump() helper's 60 s deadline cannot fire because a single update call blocks), on the macOS GitHub runner. Observed on Python 3.12.10 / Tk 8.6.16 and Python 3.13.16 / Tk 8.6.18 (Actions runs 41051795559, 41076365906, 41078379331); the same suite passes 656/656 on Python 3.14.x / Tk 9.0.4 on the runner and 3.14.6 / Tk 9.0 locally. Because pytest-timeout's thread method kills the process at the hang, the tests after it were never reached on Tk 8.6, so there may be more problems there. Not known whether it is a test-harness problem (pump + the recorded messagebox) or the GUI itself blocking on Tk 8.6.
findings.disposition_reason: Low-findings triage 2026-11-05: Obsolete: the Python/tkinter GUI this finding is about was removed (e0a58e8), so there is no Tk 8.6 suite left to hang.

findings.description: Intermittent on the macOS runner: TestVendorOps::test_exit_1_is_a_plain_failure_and_its_text_is_shown_once failed once on Python 3.14.9 / Tk 9.0.4 (Actions run 41077651429, 655 of 656 passed) because the CLI's captured stderr was not exactly 'Error: camera busy': macOS's CoreFoundation fork-safety message ('The process has forked and you cannot use this CoreFoundation functionality safely. You MUST exec(). Break on __THE_PROCESS_HAS_FORKED_AND_YOU_CANNOT_USE_THIS_COREFOUNDATION_FUNCTIONALITY___YOU_MUST_EXEC__() to debug.', printed twice) appeared ahead of it in the text the GUI shows. It did not recur on 3.14 in runs 41076365906, 41078379331 or 41081841703, nor in repeated local runs on Tk 9.0, so about 1 failure in 4 CI runs. The GUI shows the CLI's stderr verbatim in its error dialogs, so if the message comes from the process the GUI spawns, a user could see it too; it is not known whether it comes from the forked child before exec (the GUI/Tk parent has Cocoa loaded) or from the fake CLI the test runs.
findings.disposition_reason: Low-findings triage 2026-11-05: Obsolete: the Python/tkinter GUI and its fleet_cli.py were removed (e0a58e8); the egui GUI spawns the CLI with a different path and none of its tests showed the CoreFoundation fork message.

findings.description: SFTP status mapping: NoSuchFile always FolderMissing; other statuses go to step default — NoSuchFile on Download/Delete after our own upload succeeded is rare. DUP-OF F40 for the NoSuchFile part; NoConnection/ConnectionLost mapped to the step default is extra.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in remediation run nikon-fleet-remediate-20261106-a4c7. Code fixes carry tests that were run against a mutation of the fix and failed; doc/comment/label-only fixes have no test. Nothing verified on a camera, a real FTP/SFTP server or a GUI screen.

findings.description: SFTP auth/channel/subsystem transport errors classed inconsistently — Auth transport errors become HandshakeFailed; channel-open errors become Other. Message is shown. Hint quality only.
findings.disposition_reason: See 140.

findings.description: Discarded quit/close results; clock-before-epoch name; trimmed vs untrimmed folder — quit/close after the verdict is tolerable. unwrap_or(0) still leaves the pid in the name. Trim difference is DUP-OF F41.
findings.disposition_reason: Folder trim covered by 76; discarded quit/close results now commented; the pid-in-name edge left.

findings.description: Every resolver error becomes NameNotFound ("check the spelling") — An offline computer gets a spelling hint, but the OS error text is in the message. Only hostnames hit it, not IPs. Low is mainly "rare today". Disconnected reported as timeout is unreachable in practice.
findings.disposition_reason: std exposes nothing to tell resolver failures apart; the hint now says "and that this computer is online" (pinned by a test).

findings.description: io_kind folds reset/abort/EOF/InvalidData into NotThisProtocol — Also applies to mid-session errors (data connection reset after a good login), where "check protocol and port" is wrong. Message shown. Low mainly because it needs a real network fault.

findings.description: from_utf8_lossy on reply text unflagged; some FtpError variants fold to step default — Display text only; a lossy replacement char in a message nobody parses.
findings.disposition_reason: The lossy text is display-only and honest about invalid bytes.

findings.description: Category/SkipKind closed enums have no catch-all in the plan mirror — Skew needs a stale CLI; failure mode is a plan that will not parse, which fails safe (no write). Comment's "fails to compile here" is overstated but harmless. Partly DUP-OF F65 (serde(other) comment drift).

findings.description: file_left_behind holds only the bare file name — The report header prints the folder and SFTP prints the resolved path in the Folder line, so the user can find it. FTP prints the folder as typed. Minor usability.

findings.description: Runtime-build failure under Connect; channel/subsystem failures under Folder — Misattributed step on rare failures; message explains. The unjustified `let _ = tx.send` is harmless (receiver gone after timeout).
findings.disposition_reason: There is no step for opening the SFTP subsystem and the messages name what failed.

findings.description: ExtActionJson::Unknown discards the raw action tag — Unknown action blocks apply (blocked_reason), so only diagnostics are lost. Needs stale CLI to occur. Partly DUP-OF F65.
findings.disposition_reason: Keeping the raw action tag for an unknown outcome needs a hand-written Deserialize for ExtActionJson::Unknown (serde other drops it); diagnostics only and only against a stale CLI. Low value.

findings.description: Name collision / overwrite of a pre-existing file — Name is pid plus nanosecond timestamp; a collision needs a clock before 1970 plus the same pid, effectively impossible. No existence check, but that is not exposed today.
findings.disposition_reason: A temp-name collision needs a pre-1970 clock plus an identical pid; effectively impossible.

findings.description: ExtOutcomeJson::Unknown shown at Warn while Indeterminate is Error — Text already says check the camera against the restore point; status still comes from the typed report status (ApplyStatus), which drives the headline level. Needs stale CLI.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed in remediation run nikon-fleet-remediate-20261106-a4c7. Code fixes carry tests that were run against a mutation of the fix and failed; doc/comment/label-only fixes have no test. Nothing verified on a camera, a real FTP/SFTP server or a GUI screen.

findings.description: Host key copied to the report only if the handshake succeeds — The key is only informational and is not trusted or checked. A failed handshake loses a fingerprint the user could not act on anyway. PASV address not recorded: informational.
findings.disposition_reason: The SFTP host key is informational and reported-not-checked by design; the docs and GUI say so.

findings.description: plan_iptc ignores snapshot IptcStore.truncated; doc promises ListTruncated skip — Needs count >32 IPTC slots (IPTC_READ_MAX=32); bodies have 13. Doc/behaviour mismatch only. Slots absent from the snapshot are intentionally not touched.
findings.disposition_reason: IPTC slots are independent, so a truncated prefix is restored slot by slot; the doc claim of a ListTruncated skip was removed and a test pins slot-by-slot restore.

findings.description: Read-failure/undecodable states collapse into generic "no value"/"not read" skip texts — Skip still prevents the write; only the reason text loses the recorded tag/detail. Misleading text, no data effect.

findings.description: same_body skips serial compare when live USB serial is empty — Wrong-body write needs a body whose USB serial descriptor is unreadable AND a same-model body: with several bodies and no serial, open() refuses (AmbiguousDevice); the digest also binds the target serial. Real Nikon bodies report serials. id-N snapshots cause false refusals (F54), not wrong writes.
findings.disposition_reason: Fail-safe: the digest binds the target serial and several bodies without serials are refused at open.

scope: follow-up to nikon-fleet-remediate-20261106-a4c7: the three Medium findings it left deferred at the owner's request (#39 capability table + single-delete rebuild, #43 shared restore window, #45 edits off the UI thread)

findings.description: model/firmware facts hard-coded by name list; delete-all built on research probe_ftp_op — ptp_usb.rs:124-251 lists use "Z 9"/"Z6_3" strings (2 spellings); FTP_ABSENT/IPTC_ABSENT decided by name; delete_all_ftp_profiles uses FtpProbeConsent. Some drift guards exist (ptp_usb.rs:5331,8945), not all lists.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed 2026-11-06 per owner decisions: one const capability table (src/ptp_usb/model_caps.rs) read by every per-model gate, planner and capture skip; an unrecognized model is reported as not recognized and nothing is sent; the product path no longer uses delete-all (0x90EA): the FTP rebuild deletes one profile at a time with 0x90EF, highest index first, count checked after each, refusal-before-any-delete Failed, anything later Indeterminate. 25 mutations run, 22 killed; the 2 survivors are equivalent on the real table (every row that confirms writes also confirms deletes) and the column is pinned by a synthetic-row test. The new delete loop has NOT run on a body (0x90EF itself was confirmed on the Z 9 and Z6III in earlier sittings). Residual: the UnconfirmedModel message cannot name the capability (variant has no field; would need exit_status.rs and gui); src/code_policy.rs and src/range_policy.rs keep their own MAID range-copy lists (different concern).

findings.description: GUI restore_ext and CLI/worker restore-extended duplicate flows; blocked_reason vs check_ext_plan_is_for — Large copies of ui_restore/RestoreFlow; two checks of the plan-count invariant with different wording. Part REFUTED: ExtActionJson `Unknown` is visible and blocks confirmation (restore_ext.rs:32-60), its comment is accurate.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed 2026-11-06 at the owner's request. Correction to the earlier deferral text: this did not need a GUI sitting; the GUI is tested with synthetic egui input events. The window layer both restore windows carried is now one GuardedWindow in gui/src/guarded.rs (~250 duplicated lines removed from each file), one count_disagreement per plan kind, and a parity test feeds the same 39 events to both windows and requires identical transitions. Mutations (forced applicable, busy check removed, data-dir check removed, ConfirmApply ignored, count rule weakened) each fail tests. Not seen on a screen.

findings.description: every committed edit re-runs a full view load and does synchronous disk I/O on the UI thread — gui/src/main.rs:721-733, snapshot_editor.rs:123-146; edit_in_place clones+deep-compares the whole snapshot; data dir may be on /Volumes/Files. Frame freeze per edit; hot interactive path.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed 2026-11-06 at the owner's request. Correction to the earlier deferral text: not blocked on a GUI sitting. apply_viewer_edit runs the writer on a thread and reports through a ViewEditDone event; one edit in flight per window (a second is refused with a notice, never queued, so edits cannot reorder), controls disabled while saving, answers for a closed or reopened window dropped by ticket. Five mutations (guard removed, ticket check removed, controls_enabled ignoring saving, edit run inline, error notice dropped) each fail tests; one more I ran myself (controls_enabled) fails 3. Gap: the line that passes controls_enabled into the draw calls is not mutation-covered. Whether it feels responsive is untested; the owner said to revisit if not.

scope: follow-up to nikon-fleet-remediate-20261106-c9e2: the last two Medium findings from review f2c9 (#17 restore-ext in retention, #30 new FTP profile defaults)

findings.description: restore-ext restore point hand-built, bypasses make_restore_point/retention cap — restore_extended.rs:823-830 label "restore-ext"; retention::kind_of_label only knows "mcp-restore-" so cap never applies, files with plaintext FTP passwords accumulate, list_snapshots prefix misses them. One file per user-triggered apply.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed 2026-11-06 at the owner's request (the earlier "needs a retention change" deferral was not a real obstacle). RESTORE_POINT_LABEL moved into retention.rs; kind_of_label is the single classifier (equality for restore-ext, prefix for mcp-restore-); the extended-restore cap consumes retention::count_for_camera; list_snapshots gained a kind filter (label_prefix is unchanged and still misses restore-ext, tested); the cap refusal says "restore points" and how to remove them by hand; nothing is deleted automatically. restore-ext is now also a reserved label for edited copies (documented, not separately tested). Mutations (restore-ext dropped from the classifier, equality->starts_with, retain_kind keeping unreadable entries, wording reverted, MCP kind filter removed/swapped) each fail tests.

findings.description: new/duplicated FTP profiles start from the capture rig's camera network and option bits — ftp_edit.rs:209-221 template() = encode_ftp_profile with FtpCameraNetwork::CAPTURED (192.168.66.87/24). restore-extended can write it to any body. Docs "Not verified" names the template but not this value.
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed 2026-11-06 at the owner's request. A new profile no longer carries the capture rig's 192.168.66.87/24: it has no stored camera address (0.0.0.0/0) and 2.4 GHz tag kind 0x30, the form of the camera-made fixture hotspot_no_address; the combination with 5 GHz kind 4 is not itself in any fixture, the strict decoder accepts it, option bits 0x0005 and ports 21/8080 are unchanged. A duplicate copies its source whole. vendor-write-ftp still requires the captured network (tested). UNVERIFIED on a camera: whether a body accepts and connects with a profile with no stored address (check: add a profile in the editor, restore it, see whether the camera lists it and can connect). Mutations (template back to CAPTURED, kind byte left at 1, prefix 24, duplicate resetting the address, old add-note wording, gate accepting any address) each fail tests.

scope: follow-up: #73 SFTP folder check without listing the folder

findings.description: SFTP folder check lists the whole directory — ftp_test.rs:613 read_dir; large camera upload folder costs time/memory, not correctness. [also found by the Phase 2 inventory as V45]
findings.disposition_reason: Fixed 2026-11-06 at the owner's suggestion (do not list the whole folder). The SFTP folder step now does a STAT and reads the file-type bits (folder / file / link / other); a server whose answer has no type bits (none, or only rwx bits) is asked the old way by opening and reading the folder. Four mutations (always list, file accepted as folder, rwx-only mode taken as not-a-folder, no fallback) each fail tests. UNVERIFIED against a real SFTP server: whether real servers answer STAT with type bits (the fallback covers the case they do not); to be checked in the hardware/server sitting.
